target.title: fix(media): normalizeMediaSource should handle uppercase FILE:// URI schemes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`MEDIA:` directives using an uppercase `FILE://` URI scheme are left in assistant text instead of being extracted as local media attachments. Per RFC 3986, URI schemes are case-insensitive, so `MEDIA:FILE:///tmp/generated.png` should produce the same result as `MEDIA:file:///tmp/generated.png`.

Issue: #103473

## Why This Change Was Made

`normalizeMediaSource` only matched lowercase `file://` via `String.startsWith`, so uppercase and mixed-case schemes were not recognized. The remaining scheme-shaped value failed local-path validation and the directive stayed in visible output text.

## User Impact

When an assistant or tool output emits a valid file URI with non-lowercase scheme spelling, the intended local media attachment is silently not delivered and the raw directive remains in the reply. The fix makes extraction case-insensitive—no behavioral change for the common lowercase case.

## Evidence

- 59/59 tests pass (2 new cases added for uppercase `FILE://` and lowercase `file://`)
- `normalizeMediaSource("FILE:///tmp/generated.png")` now returns `/tmp/generated.png` instead of `FILE:///tmp/generated.png`
- Existing lowercase `file://` behavior unchanged

```diff
+            C12345678: { enabled: true, requireMention: true },
```

target.body:
## Summary

- Default Active Memory to configured OpenClaw agents when `plugins.entries.active-memory.config.agents` is omitted.
- Fall back to the implicit `main` agent for minimal configs that do not define `agents.list`.
- Preserve explicit empty `config.agents: []` as no targeted agents.
- Preserve explicit non-empty `config.agents` allowlist behavior.
- Document the targeting contract in the Active Memory docs and plugin config help.

This matters because omitting `config.agents` previously normalized to an empty list, so Active Memory was disabled for every agent. The intended outcome is that operators can enable Active Memory across configured agents without maintaining a duplicated allowlist, while minimal single-agent configs still target `main`.

Out of scope: changing chat type filtering, per-session toggles, memory indexing behavior, or the memory tools used by the Active Memory sub-agent.

Review focus: whether the fallback to `agents.list[].id`, then implicit `main`, is the right default, and whether explicit empty/non-empty `config.agents` remains unchanged.

## Linked context

Closes #

Related #82528

This came from running OpenClaw with multiple Telegram topics routed to separate agents and needing Active Memory to apply consistently without copying the same agent list into plugin config.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior addressed:
  Omitting `plugins.entries.active-memory.config.agents` normalized to an empty allowlist, so Active Memory skipped every agent instead of applying to configured agents.
- Real environment tested:
  OpenClaw 2026.6.5 on a Linux host with a systemd user gateway, Telegram group topics routed to `main`, `sementes`, `cloudfarm`, and `pedro-agenda`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  Applied the equivalent runtime change locally, removed `active-memory.config.agents`, restarted `openclaw-gateway`, then checked gateway status and memory search.
- Evidence after fix:

```text
openclaw gateway status --deep
Gateway version: 2026.6.5
Runtime: running
Capability: admin-capable
```

```text
journalctl --user -u openclaw-gateway --since "3 minutes ago"
[gateway] http server listening (12 plugins: active-memory, brave, browser, canvas, codex, device-pair, file-transfer, memory-core, openai, phone-control, talk-voice, telegram; 12.1s)
```

```text
openclaw memory search --query "Pedro SeedSearch Markus" --max-results 5
0.545 memory/pendencias-grupo.md:1-21
0.516 memory/2026-03-31.md:1-37
0.453 memory/dreaming/light/2026-06-05.md:43-72
```

- Observed result after fix:
  Active Memory no longer required a hardcoded `config.agents` list to apply across configured agents.
- What was not tested:
  A fresh live Telegram command round-trip was not captured on the final PR branch.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints:
  The production server was restored to upstream behavior after proof collection, using an explicit `config.agents` list until this PR is merged upstream.
- Before evidence:
  Reading the prior plugin implementation showed `normalizePluginConfig({}).agents` became `[]`, while `isEnabledForAgent` requires `config.agents.includes(agentId)`.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:

```text

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

node --import tsx -e "import { testing } from './extensions/active-memory/index.ts'; const cfg={agents:{list:[{id:'main'},{id:'support'}]}}; console.log(JSON.stringify({ omitted: testing.normalizePluginConfig({}, cfg).agents, empty: testing.normalizePluginConfig({agents: []}, cfg).agents, explicit: testing.normalizePluginConfig({agents:['support']}, cfg).agents, implicitMain: testing.normalizePluginConfig({}).agents }, null, 2));"
git diff --check upstream/main -- docs/concepts/active-memory.md extensions/active-memory/index.ts extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts extensions/active-memory/openclaw.plugin.json
.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode commit --commit HEAD
```

Regression coverage added:

- `defaults to all configured agents when no active-memory agent allowlist is set`
- `preserves an empty active-memory agent allowlist`
- `defaults to the implicit main agent when no agent list is configured`
- `keeps an explicit active-memory agent allowlist`

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes`)

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes`)

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`No`)

Highest-risk area:

target.title: test(firecrawl): cover Unicode error boundaries
target.body:
## Summary

- Preserve UTF-16 surrogate pairs when Firecrawl truncates non-success HTTP error details.
- Add a loopback HTTP regression through the public Firecrawl search entry point.
- Keep the regression's asynchronous server cleanup compatible with bundled extension lint.

## What Problem This Solves

`postFirecrawlJson()` is the source-of-truth formatter for Firecrawl's non-success response detail before it is wrapped and exposed in an `Error`. Its fixed `detail.slice(0, 1_000)` limit counts UTF-16 code units, so a detail with 999 ASCII code units followed by an astral Unicode character retains only that character's high surrogate. The emitted error text is therefore malformed even though the upstream JSON body is valid.

Current `origin/main` still contains the raw truncation:

```text
origin/main=54769305682df2bfd89b7fb9f204d76acbcea387
extensions/firecrawl/src/firecrawl-client.ts:247
const safeDetail = wrapWebContent(detail.slice(0, 1_000), "web_fetch");
```

## User Impact

When a Firecrawl search or scrape request receives a long JSON, status-text, or non-JSON HTTP failure detail at this boundary, users can receive malformed Unicode in the surfaced error. The error stays bounded at the existing limit while retaining valid text encoding.

## Origin / follow-up

Follows #102949.

Gap this fills: the same fixed-width UTF-16 truncation pattern remained in Firecrawl's shared HTTP-error formatter.

Consistency: this reuses the existing public `truncateUtf16Safe` plugin SDK helper rather than introducing another Unicode-boundary policy.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

The current open-PR scan checked changes to `extensions/firecrawl/src/firecrawl-client.ts` and `extensions/firecrawl/src/firecrawl-client.test.ts`; no other open PR covers this truncation point.

```json
[]
```

This patch is limited to the Firecrawl HTTP error-detail boundary and its colocated regression path.

## Merge risk

- **Why it matters / User impact:** Prevents malformed Unicode in a user-visible Firecrawl failure path while retaining the existing bounded-error behavior.
- **Risk labels considered:** None.
- **Risk explanation:** At a surrogate boundary, the helper can retain one fewer UTF-16 code unit than raw `slice()`; that is the minimum change needed to avoid emitting an invalid standalone surrogate.
- **Why acceptable:** The 1,000-code-unit limit, response parsing, endpoint policy, wrapper, and final error format are unchanged. Only an invalid Unicode boundary is moved backward.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High; the source-of-truth formatter now uses the repository's existing UTF-16-safe helper, the public runtime path has focused regression and loopback HTTP proof, and the exact CI lint failure introduced by that regression was reproduced and repaired locally.
- **Patch quality notes:** The production diff changes one truncation call. The regression's server cleanup was expanded solely to satisfy `no-promise-executor-return`; it does not add a fallback, catch, configuration path, or protocol change.
- **Target test file:** `extensions/firecrawl/src/firecrawl-client.test.ts` runs the regression through `runFirecrawlSearch()` and a real loopback HTTP response.
- **Root cause:** The source-of-truth `postFirecrawlJson()` error formatter used raw UTF-16 code-unit slicing after it had selected a valid string from status text, JSON `error`/`message`, or a text body. Its fixed boundary can divide a surrogate pair before the user-visible error is constructed.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The invariant belongs at the shared formatter: every non-success Firecrawl detail reaches the same truncation operation before `wrapWebContent()` and `Error` construction. Replacing that operation with the established safe helper fixes the invalid-boundary source for JSON, status-text, and text-body detail inputs rather than sanitizing an already malformed downstream error.
- **What did NOT change:** This does not change Firecrawl authentication, configuration schema/type, secret resolution, endpoint validation, request payloads, cache behavior, response selection precedence, error wrapper format, or scrape-result truncation; unrelated behavior is out of scope.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `postFirecrawlJson()` is the source-of-truth plugin boundary for non-success HTTP error formatting. The plugin consumes the public `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime` contract; endpoint and configuration validation remain in their existing owner modules.
- **Scenario locked in:** A real loopback `/v2/search` response returns HTTP 400 JSON with `x × 999 + 🚀 + tail`, placing the 1,000th UTF-16 code unit inside the rocket surrogate pair.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** One `truncateUtf16Safe(detail, 1_000)` substitution protects all detail-source variants owned by this formatter without altering their parsing or their shared 1,000-unit policy.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A Firecrawl HTTP error detail no longer ends in a lone high surrogate when the existing 1,000-unit formatter boundary bisects an astral Unicode character.
- **Canonical reachability path:** User-configured `plugins.entries.firecrawl.config.webSearch` input → `OpenClawConfig` plugin configuration type and record ingestion → `resolveFirecrawlApiKey()` secret-input normalization plus `resolveFirecrawlBaseUrl()` trim/default normalization and endpoint validation → runtime `runFirecrawlSearch()` request object → `resolveEndpoint()` and `postFirecrawlJson()` HTTP request/effect → response detail parsing → wrapped thrown `Error`.
- **Boundary crossed:** Local runtime and HTTP boundary: the actual Firecrawl search runtime issued a POST to a loopback self-hosted `/v2/search` endpoint, which returned a 400 JSON error body that reached the final thrown `Error`.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reviewed the existing public plugin SDK text utility and reused its shared `truncateUtf16Safe` helper. The helper is applied only to the formatter's existing 1,000-unit limit; no provider range, endpoint, credential, or configuration constraint changes.
- **Real environment tested:** Node 22, the OpenClaw Firecrawl plugin, and a local HTTP server bound to `127.0.0.1` using the plugin's supported self-hosted `webSearch.baseUrl` configuration seam.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `pnpm test extensions/firecrawl/src/firecrawl-client.test.ts`; `pnpm run lint:extensions:bundled`; then `node_modules/.bin/tsx --tsconfig tsconfig.json firecrawl-utf16-proof.ts`, which starts the loopback server and invokes public `runFirecrawlSearch()` with the boundary payload.
- **Evidence after fix:** `firecrawl-regression-after-ci-fix.txt` records 53 passing focused tests; `ci-repro-lint-after-fix.txt` records the CI-equivalent bundled lint passing; `firecrawl-e2e-after-ci-fix.txt` records the public runtime path, loopback POST, and final error check.
- **Observed result after fix:** The request reached `/v2/search`; the terminal `Error` check reported `hasLoneHighSurrogate: false` with `errorLength: 1804`. The safe truncation removed the boundary-splitting code unit and preserved the surrounding bounded error behavior.
- **What was not tested:** Firecrawl SaaS was not called. This proof exercises OpenClaw's locally configurable self-hosted HTTP path and its final error formatting, not third-party service availability.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

```text
BEFORE (original origin/main runtime)
{"requestPath":"/v2/search","hasLoneHighSurrogate":true,"errorLength":1805}

AFTER (current patch runtime)
{"requestPath":"/v2/search","hasLoneHighSurrogate":false,"errorLength":1804}
```

## CI repair

The current-head CI run first failed both `check-lint` and `check-additional-extension-bundled` at the newly added test's Promise executor (`no-promise-executor-return`). The base main CI run for `0f3fb9ea58036d5080452e016196c69939520fc2` succeeded, so this was a direct PR-introduced test cleanup issue rather than a main-baseline failure.

The server-close callback now calls `resolve()` or `reject()` from a block body. `ci-repro-lint-before-fix.txt` reproduces the same failure locally and `ci-repro-lint-after-fix.txt` records the same CI command passing after the minimal adjustment.

## Regression Test Plan

- Run `pnpm test extensions/firecrawl/src/firecrawl-client.test.ts`.
- Run `pnpm run lint:extensions:bundled` to cover the bundled extension CI shard.
- Confirm a real loopback 400 JSON response with `x × 999 + 🚀 + tail` reaches the public search entry point and the final `Error` contains neither a lone high surrogate nor a replacement-character artifact.
- Retain the existing tests for endpoint policy, payload parsing, and scrape behavior unchanged.

## Risk / Compatibility

No public API, configuration schema, endpoint policy, response schema, error format, or truncation limit changes. Only at an invalid UTF-16 boundary can the rendered detail become one code unit shorter, preserving valid Unicode rather than exposing a split surrogate.

## What was not changed

No Firecrawl authentication, self-hosted endpoint policy, SSRF validation, request payload, normal response parsing, cache, or scrape-result behavior was changed.

## Root Cause

Raw `detail.slice(0, 1_000)` operates on UTF-16 code units in the shared non-success HTTP formatter. Valid upstream error strings can contain surrogate pairs, and the formatter's source-of-truth fixed boundary can split one before it is wrapped into a user-visible `Error`. Reusing `truncateUtf16Safe` preserves the existing bound while enforcing the Unicode boundary invariant at the formatter that owns it.

target.title: fix(ui): preserve lobster vigil reactions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A shy lobster can be present solely because a busy run crossed the ten-minute vigil threshold. On busy-to-idle, the component consumed that sole presence owner before reconciliation, which immediately erased the success cheer, failure droop, or abort acknowledgement and sent the lobster away. Browser-cancelled pointer gestures also left the press-and-hold timer alive, allowing a delayed pet after the interaction had ended.

Closes #103475. Follow-up to #103344 and #103573.

## Why This Change Was Made

The active terminal outcome chain now carries a closed `"vigil" | null` presence owner. It survives the current failure sequence from droop through sweep, then releases after the terminal act. Seed resets, page hiding, overrides, and forced departures release it immediately. Existing scheduled-visit and offline presence owners remain unchanged. The existing hold-cancel handler is also wired to `pointercancel`.

## User Impact

Long-running shy pets visibly finish their success, failure, or abort reaction before performing the normal leave transition. Failed runs retain the complete droop-and-sweep sequence added on current `main`. Cancelled touch or stylus interactions cannot trigger a delayed pet.

## Evidence

- Exact-current-main red proof at `dff4c634f1a56d974a1e4faaa9520527ab026774`, Testbox-through-Crabbox lease `tbx_01kx5v4kjc25srfwkq9p6j3b62`: `pnpm test ui/src/components/lobster-pet.test.ts` failed exactly four new regressions (pointer cancel plus vigil-only success, failure, and abort), while 48 existing tests passed.

- Real Chromium proof: `ui/src/e2e/lobster-pet.e2e.test.ts`, 2/2 passed with a paused Playwright clock, covering terminal outcome timing and native `pointercancel` wiring.
- Broad Control UI proof: `pnpm test:ui:e2e`, 34 files and 108 tests passed.
- `pnpm format:check -- ui/src/components/lobster-pet.ts ui/src/components/lobster-pet.test.ts ui/src/e2e/lobster-pet.e2e.test.ts`: passed.

target.title: fix(ios): trim model names in model picker
target.body:
Closes #103365

## What Problem This Solves

The iOS model picker shows model names with untrimmed leading/trailing whitespace when the gateway's model catalog returns a padded `name` (e.g. `"  Claude Opus 4  "`). This can misalign or truncate the label in the SwiftUI picker row. Model selection itself is unaffected since `modelID` is separate.

## Why This Change Was Made

`IOSGatewayChatTransport.decodeModelChoices` (`apps/ios/Sources/Chat/IOSGatewayChatTransport.swift:298`) already computes a trimmed `name` and uses it for the is-it-blank check, but the non-empty branch returned the untrimmed `model.name` instead of the already-trimmed local `name`. Fixed to return the trimmed value, which was already in hand.

## User Impact

iOS users see the model name rendered without stray padding in the model picker, matching what the app already computes and displays for the blank-name fallback case.

## Evidence

- [x] Extended `apps/ios/Tests/IOSGatewayChatTransportTests.swift` with a `"  Claude Opus 4  "` case that only fails on the untrimmed path (the existing suite only covered a fully-blank name, where both expressions happened to agree).

target.title: fix(slack): read resolved userToken with env fallback in channel type resolution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveSlackConversationInfo()` uses `account.config.userToken` to resolve the token for Slack API calls. `account.config.userToken` only contains the raw config value — it does **not** include the `SLACK_USER_TOKEN` environment variable fallback.

Users who set `SLACK_USER_TOKEN` env var without also configuring `channels.slack.accounts.<id>.userToken` in the config file get an empty token, causing channel type resolution to silently fall back to `"unknown"` for non-DM channels.

## Changes

- `channel-type.ts:88`: `account.config.userToken` → `account.userToken`
- `account.userToken` is the resolved value that includes env fallback (`configUser ?? envUser`)

## Evidence

target.title: fix: protect SMS webhook callback quota [AI]
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where invalid SMS webhook posts could consume the same inbound callback quota used by signed Twilio callbacks when deployments receive traffic through a shared proxy address.

## Why This Change Was Made

The SMS webhook now parses and validates Twilio-signed form requests, confirms the configured account, and only then applies the fixed-window quota. The quota key is scoped to the SMS account and webhook route plus the client address so one account path cannot consume another account path's quota.

## User Impact

Operators using the SMS plugin keep the same Twilio signature validation and webhook responses, while invalid unsigned traffic no longer burns the quota for later valid callbacks. High-volume valid signed callbacks are still rate-limited per account route.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs run --provider aws --idle-timeout 90m --ttl 240m --timing-json --shell -- "corepack pnpm test extensions/sms/src/webhook.test.ts"`

target.title: fix(acp): abort controller in clearActiveRun to match cancelActiveRun contract
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`clearActiveRun` discards the AbortController without calling `.abort()`. Any asynchronous operation holding a reference to the controller's signal will not receive a cancellation notification and will continue running to completion, wasting resources.

In the same file `cancelActiveRun` correctly calls `.abort()` before setting the controller to null. `removeSession` also does the right thing. The omission in `clearActiveRun` is a one-line gap.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `session.abortController?.abort()` so `clearActiveRun` matches the behaviour of `cancelActiveRun` and `removeSession`.

## User Impact

No visible impact for normal workflows. When `clearActiveRun` is called to release an active run without explicit cancellation, downstream async work that checks `signal.aborted` will now correctly observe the termination instead of silently continuing.

## Evidence

```
$ pnpm test packages/acp-core/src/session.test.ts -- --run
 ✓ 11 passed  (10 existing + 1 new)
```

target.body:
## Summary

- preserve legitimate iOS share text that merely starts with a historical scaffold marker such as `Text:`
- keep removing standalone scaffold lines case-insensitively
- extract the pure sanitizer so the regression is covered by focused logic tests

## Issue / Motivation

Fixes #103364.

The Share Extension treated scaffold strings as prefixes, so valid shared content such as `Text: the quick brown fox` was silently removed from the draft. Scaffold removal should apply only when an entire trimmed line matches a known marker.

## Changes

- move draft-fragment cleanup into `ShareDraftSanitizer`
- replace prefix matching with exact, case-insensitive line matching
- remove the redundant malformed scaffold entry
- add focused tests for standalone markers, legitimate prefixed text, and multiline cleanup

## Testing

- `git diff --check` — passed

## What Problem This Solves

The iOS Share Extension no longer drops legitimate user content solely because a line begins with `Text:` or another scaffold phrase. Exact historical scaffold lines are still removed, preserving the original cleanup behavior without prefix-based data loss.

## Evidence

Before this change, the sanitizer rejected `lowered.hasPrefix(marker)`, so both `Text: the quick brown fox` and `TEXT: legitimate` became empty. The focused regression cases now assert that those strings remain intact while exact mixed-case `tExT:` is removed and multiline content removes only the exact scaffold line.

target.title: fix(security): avoid false-positive secret findings when config uses env references
target.body:
<!--
Closes #62438
-->

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw security audit` reported `config.secrets.gateway_password_in_config` (warn) and `config.secrets.hooks_token_in_config` (info) for values that correctly use the documented `${ENV_VAR}` substitution syntax.

## Why This Change Was Made

The secrets-in-config collector was checking the resolved runtime config, where `${...}` placeholders had already been substituted by the config loader. `ConfigFileSnapshot.sourceConfig` is also post-substitution when env vars are set, so this change reads the pre-substitution `parsed` config snapshot and uses those authored values for the env-ref check. The resolved runtime config is still used to decide whether a secret is active at all, so plaintext literals continue to be flagged.

## User Impact

Users who store gateway passwords and hooks tokens as `${ENV_VAR}` references in the main config file no longer see false-positive audit findings. Plaintext literals in config are still flagged.

## Evidence

- Added regression tests in `src/security/audit-config-basics.test.ts` covering both env-ref suppression and continued plaintext flagging, using an explicit `configSnapshot` with pre-substitution `parsed` values.
- Targeted test runs: `pnpm test src/security/audit-config-basics.test.ts` and `pnpm test src/cli/security-cli.test.ts` pass.

target.title: fix(http): accept repeated content-length values
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Some external HTTP response readers still rejected comma-joined duplicate `Content-Length` headers such as `"10, 10"`. That shape can be produced by HTTP stacks/proxies when duplicate identical headers are merged, and `packages/media-core` already treats matching repeated values as valid while still rejecting conflicting or malformed values.

This caused unnecessary failures for otherwise valid responses in three bounded download/feed paths:

- Marketplace plugin archive downloads
- Hosted official external plugin catalog feeds
- Gateway model pricing catalog refreshes

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix reuses the existing `parseMediaContentLength()` helper instead of keeping three slightly different local parsers. This preserves the existing byte limits and malformed-header failures, while accepting only repeated values whose trimmed decimal bytes match exactly.

## User Impact

Users avoid false failures when a CDN/proxy returns an equivalent repeated `Content-Length` value. Oversized, unsafe, malformed, or conflicting lengths are still rejected before streaming or parsing the body.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(slack): time out stalled external file uploads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where sending a file to Slack could leave the entire message delivery waiting indefinitely when Slack's external upload URL stopped responding after the media buffer had already been loaded into memory.

## Why This Change Was Made

The binary POST to Slack's presigned upload URL now uses the existing timeout and guarded-fetch paths with a 120-second total budget, matching the bounded media-transfer behavior already used by Slack inbound media and other attachment delivery paths. Timeout diagnostics receive only the upload origin, so Slack's path-bearing upload capability is not written to logs. This does not change Slack API negotiation, completion calls, retries, SSRF policy, configuration, or message payloads.

## User Impact

Stalled Slack file uploads now fail within a bounded interval instead of holding an in-memory media buffer and the delivery queue indefinitely. Successful uploads continue through the existing completion flow unchanged.

## Evidence

- Regression proof: the new hanging-upload test failed before the production change because the guarded upload call had no finite timeout.
- Focused Slack upload suite: `12 passed`; enterprise Slack send suite: `13 passed`. The focused suite also verifies that a path-bearing presigned capability is reduced to its origin before it reaches timeout logging.
- Local changed-file lanes passed, including extension production/test typechecks, changed-file lint, import cycles, dependency guards, and conflict-marker checks.
- Near-real production boundary proof: a real local media file followed the production `uploadSlackFile` and guarded-fetch path to a hanging HTTP `POST /upload`. The 120,000ms budget raised `TimeoutError: request timed out` after 120,183ms, closed the response, and left `files.completeUploadExternal` uncalled. The warning logged only the Slack origin, not the synthetic capability path. Slack upload-URL negotiation and destination routing were substituted because this environment has no Slack workspace credentials; the media load, binary POST, timeout signal, logging path, and socket cancellation used the production path.

  ```text
  fetch timeout after 120000ms (elapsed 120001ms) operation=slack-upload-file url=https://uploads.slack.com/
  route=POST /upload
  elapsedMs=120183
  error=TimeoutError: request timed out
  responseClosed=true
  completeUploadCalls=0
  ```

- Latest `origin/main` still lacked a timeout on the external binary POST before this patch; open PR searches for `upload_url`, `getUploadURLExternal`, and the reported timeout found no competing fix. PR #102635 touches the same delivery module for native charts but does not change file uploads.

target.title: fix(slack): use endsWith instead of includes for _all_ action_id matching
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`isBulkActionsBlock()` uses `el.action_id.includes("_all_")` to detect bulk-action buttons. This has **two bugs**:

1. **False positives**: Action IDs like `"deploy_all_services"` or `"install_all_deps"` contain the substring `_all_` and are incorrectly treated as bulk actions — their blocks are silently removed from Slack messages.
2. **False negatives**: Legitimate bulk action IDs like `"select_all"` / `"deselect_all"` do **not** contain `_all_` (no trailing underscore), so `includes("_all_")` fails to match them.

## Changes

- `interactions.block-actions.ts:293`: `includes("_all_")` → `endsWith("_all")`
- `+1/-1` change

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users signing in to GitHub Copilot could remain rate-limited until their device code expired after GitHub returned `slow_down`. GitHub Copilot device login can recover from rate-limit backoff without repeatedly polling too quickly or waiting until the authorization code expires.

target.title: fix(sessions): guard sessions.create fork against cross-plugin ownership bypass
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions.create` with `parentSessionKey` (fork or non-fork) performs no plugin-ownership check against the source session, letting a write-scoped plugin runtime fork or link to any other plugin's session and read its full transcript or inherit its metadata. `sessions.delete` already enforces this check via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`; `sessions.create` does not.

- **Problem**: Plugin B can call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "pluginA's key" })` and receive a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Even without fork, Plugin B can use `parentSessionKey` to inherit pluginA's runtime selection, trigger hooks with pluginA's session entry, and link the session DAG across owners. The equivalent `sessions.delete` call against the same source session is correctly refused.
- **Solution**: Add a unified ownership check in `createGatewaySession` — when the caller has a `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`, reject *any* parent-session use (fork or non-fork) unless the parent session's `pluginOwnerId` matches. Ownerless (user) sessions are also protected, consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`.
- **What changed**: `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts` (unified ownership check + `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` param), `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` (pass `client.internal.pluginRuntimeOwnerId`), `src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts` (full scenario matrix)
- **What did NOT change**: Non-plugin clients (no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`) are unaffected; plugins using their own sessions as parent continue to work.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #103089
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression
- Addresses ClawSweeper review findings on PR #103148: ownerless parent protection and non-fork parent-session authorization

## Motivation

Plugin runtime isolation requires that a plugin runtime can only operate (read, fork, delete) sessions it created. `sessions.delete` correctly enforces this via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch()`. The `sessions.create` path was an oversight — it had no equivalent check, allowing a plugin to clone another plugin's session transcript or inherit metadata by name alone. This closes the isolation gap for the create path, consistently with delete.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: sessions.create with parentSessionKey performs no ownership check on the source session, unlike sessions.delete
- Environment: Linux (kernel 4.19.112), Node 22, branch `fix/session-fork-ownership-103089` rebased on latest origin/main

**Full regression suite:**

```bash
pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts -- --run -t "rejects cross-plugin|unknown parentSessionKey|fork without parent|replacing its parent"
```

```console
 Tests  8 passed | 48 skipped (56)
```

**Ownership check test matrix (7 scenarios):**

| Scenario | fork? | Parent owner | Caller | Result |
|----------|-------|-------------|--------|--------|
| Plugin B forks Plugin A's session | ✅ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST`: "cannot use session ... as parent" |
| Plugin B forks ownerless (user) session | ✅ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` — consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` |
| Non-plugin client forks any session | ✅ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> Plugin A's session | ❌ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> ownerless session | ❌ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> own session | ❌ | `pluginB` | `pluginB` | ✅ Success — ownership confirmed |
| Non-plugin client non-fork parent | ❌ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check (covered by existing tests) |

- Observed result after fix:
  1. **Cross-plugin fork**: `createGatewaySession({ ..., pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB" })` with a `pluginOwnerId: "pluginA"` parent returns `{ ok: false, error: { code: "INVALID_REQUEST", message: "Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it." } }`
  2. **Non-plugin clients** are unaffected — they have no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` so the check skips entirely
  3. **Self-ownership**: Plugin forking/parenting its own session succeeds
  4. **Ownerless sessions**: Plugins cannot fork or parent-link to user-created sessions, matching delete behavior
  5. **No regression**: All existing fork tests continue to pass
- What was not tested: cross-store fork (`targetStorePath`); live gateway RPC over WebSocket transport

## Root Cause (if applicable)

`sessions.create` handler in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` passes `parentSessionKey` to `createGatewaySession` in `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts`, which resolves the parent session entry but never checks `entry.pluginOwnerId` against the caller's `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`. The matching ownership check (`rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`) exists for `sessions.delete` but was never mirrored in the create path.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

Comprehensive test `"sessions.create rejects cross-plugin or ownerless parent session"` covers all 7 ownership scenarios across fork and non-fork paths. Existing fork tests continue to pass.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None for end users. Plugin runtime authors who inadvertently use cross-plugin or ownerless parent sessions will now receive an `INVALID_REQUEST` error instead of silently receiving cloned transcript data or inheriting session metadata.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No — existing `operator.write` scope is sufficient for self-owned sessions
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No — only narrowed: cross-plugin and ownerless parent use is now rejected

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux 4.19.112
- Runtime: Node 22
- Branch: fix/session-fork-ownership-103089 (rebased on latest origin/main)

### Steps

1. Seed a session store entry owned by "pluginA" with a transcript
2. As a caller with `pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB"` and `operator.write` scope, call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "<pluginA's key>" })`
3. Observe the call is rejected with `INVALID_REQUEST`

### Expected

`sessions.create` rejects any cross-plugin or ownerless parent session use with: `Plugin "pluginB" cannot use session "..." as parent because it did not create it.`

### Actual (before fix)

The fork call succeeds and pluginB receives a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Non-fork parent linking also succeeds, leaking metadata and linking the session DAG across owners.

## Evidence

- [ ] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Plugin B forking Plugin A's session (rejected), Plugin B forking ownerless session (rejected), non-plugin client forking any session (allowed), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to Plugin A's session (rejected), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to ownerless session (rejected), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to own session (allowed)
- Edge cases checked: no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` (skip check), ownerless parent (reject for plugins), self-ownership (allow), `fork === false` with `parentSessionKey` (now gated)
- What you did NOT verify: Live gateway WebSocket transport; cross-store fork with `targetStorePath`

## Review Conversations

- [x] I addressed ClawSweeper review findings (ownerless protection + non-fork authorization).
- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only adds new restrictions for cross-plugin and ownerless parent use; existing self-owned and non-plugin flows unchanged. This matches existing `sessions.delete` behavior.
- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — the ownership check is placed in `createGatewaySession` at the service layer, close to where the parent session entry is resolved, rather than in the handler. This prevents future callers from accidentally bypassing the check. The unified check (fork + non-fork) mirrors `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` in delete — same rule, same surface.
- **Refactor needed**: No — the check is a self-contained change; `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` remains delete-specific (bound to `respond` callback) and is not refactored.
- **Alternative considered**: Adding the check in the `sessions.create` handler (sessions.ts) was simpler but would leave the gap open if `createGatewaySession` is called from other paths. Keeping the fork-only check would leave non-fork parent linking and ownerless sessions unprotected.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Prompt context included issue body, source-level provenance analysis of `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` and `createGatewaySession`, and ClawSweeper review discussion.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Low risk — this is an additive security hardening that narrows existing behavior. The check mirrors `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` which has been shipping since the delete path. Key mitigations:
- Non-plugin clients (the majority of callers) are entirely unaffected
- Plugin runtimes using their own sessions continue to work
- Ownerless session protection is consistent with existing delete behavior — plugins already cannot delete user sessions
- The error message follows the same pattern as `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`

**Specific change from earlier PR revision**: The guard was expanded from fork-only to all parent-session use, and ownerless sessions are now protected. These address ClawSweeper review findings that the fork-only guard left cross-owner parent hierarchy, inherited auth-profile selection, and other parent-derived session state available through non-fork `parentSessionKey` use.

target.title: fix(agents): lease session worktrees during runs
target.body:
## Summary

Session-backed managed worktrees are now leased for the lifetime of every agent run. Idle GC waits for an admitted run to finish before it can snapshot or force-remove that checkout, including when the run uses a subdirectory inside the worktree.

## Root cause

GC's owner-activity read and `git worktree remove --force` were independent operations. The previous patch repeated the read closer to removal, but a session could still be admitted after that read and while the destructive command started.

## Fix

The managed-worktree service now owns a per-worktree FIFO lease. `agent-command` acquires the lease before a session run touches its configured cwd and releases it in its outer cleanup. All managed removal paths acquire the same lease through snapshotting and git removal; idle GC retains the owner-active guard after it has obtained that lease.

Lease lookup accepts a managed worktree root or one of its subdirectories, matching session worktrees whose configured workspace is nested below the repository root.

## Why this is the right boundary

The worktree service owns the destructive operation and is the only place that can serialize it consistently with its consumers. Agent command is the session-run admission point that has the resolved cwd and can retain the lease through the actual runtime. Explicit removal keeps its existing force semantics, while an agent that loses the race before admission fails before using a deleted cwd rather than running against it.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts`: 24 passed.
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on `src/agents/agent-command.ts`, `src/agents/worktrees/service.ts`, and `src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts`: clean.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/worktree-gc-core.tsbuildinfo`: clean.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/worktree-gc-core-test.tsbuildinfo`: clean.
- Structured local review: no accepted or actionable findings.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: a resumed session must not have its managed checkout removed while its agent run is using that checkout or a nested workspace within it.
Real environment tested: pristine main `6eb9a5ada23b20353da9ef8e9fe69881567ca74f` and this patch `8a5ea1bac785439394ba6959fca805fa4231aee7`, driving the production ManagedWorktreeService against real on-disk git worktrees and filesystem state.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: create a session-owned worktree, start a lease from a nested directory, begin idle removal, confirm the directory remains present while the lease is held, release the lease, then observe the same queued removal complete.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 6eb9a5a)
nested session directory exists while removal is pending: false
queued removal completes only after the active run ends: false
# AFTER (this patch 8a5ea1b)
nested session directory exists while removal is pending: true
queued removal completes only after the active run ends: true
```
Observed result after fix: a live session retains its nested working directory until its lease ends, after which queued cleanup can complete normally.
What was not tested: no live provider request or multi-process gateway deployment was exercised; the production worktree lifecycle and real git filesystem operations were exercised in-process.

## Summary

- Adds a shared `/stream` command (alias `/streaming`) for session-scoped preview streaming mode overrides without editing channel config or restarting the gateway.
- Persists the canonical mode on `SessionEntry.streamingMode`; accepted modes are `off`, `partial`, `block`, and `progress`. The command accepts `final` as a user-facing alias for canonical `off`.
- Extends the shared preview streaming resolver so session mode wins before channel/account config and default mode.
- Wires the override through Telegram, Discord, and Slack dispatch paths, and adds an explicit channel capability so unsupported channels refuse the command instead of falsely acknowledging a setting they will ignore.
- Intentionally out of scope: `/progress` / `streaming.preview.toolProgress` from #80989, Mattermost/MS Teams/Matrix runtime wiring, and protocol/TUI patch support.

## Linked context

Closes #74077

Related #80989
Related #81009

Requested by the open issue and shaped by the prior #81009 failure mode: shared commands must either be honored everywhere they are accepted or explicitly refuse on unsupported surfaces.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: `/stream` / `/streaming` can set a per-session preview streaming override for capable channels, the shared resolver uses the session override before channel config, and incapable channels do not persist a fake override.
- Real environment tested: local OpenClaw source checkout on Linux, branch `clawsean/stream-mode-session-command`, rebased onto current `upstream/main` (`caab343461`).
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node --import tsx --input-type=module` with production `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-session.ts` and `src/plugin-sdk/channel-streaming.ts` imports; targeted Vitest; `pnpm tsgo:prod`; `pnpm check:test-types`; `git diff --check`.
- Evidence after fix: terminal capture from the production resolver/handler smoke:

```console
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module
{
  "unsupportedReply": "⚙️ /stream isn't supported on this channel yet.",
  "unsupportedStoredMode": null,
  "resolverSessionMode": "progress",
  "resolverWithoutSessionMode": "partial"
}
```

- Observed result after fix: unsupported channel handling refused `/stream` without writing `SessionEntry.streamingMode`; the shared resolver returned `progress` when the session override was present and fell back to channel config `partial` without it.
- What was not tested: live Telegram, Discord, or Slack UI behavior from a deployed gateway branch; Mattermost/MS Teams/Matrix are intentionally unsupported by the new capability gate in this PR.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: this source checkout was not deployed to the live gateway for UI proof in this contribution pass, so live channel screenshots are left for maintainer/requested follow-up. Local runtime/unit coverage covers command registration, set/status/reset, unsupported-channel refusal/no persist, resolver session precedence, and Telegram/Discord/Slack helper precedence.

target.title: feat(signal): add setup wizard
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal setup needed a guided path that proves a usable receive transport before users rely on the channel, without OpenClaw creating or managing a Signal Docker container. Existing setup and status paths could also leave stale native/container transport fields ambiguous, miss account-specific API-mode behavior, or report a Signal daemon as generically working when the configured account was missing or receive was unavailable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Signal plugin now owns a setup wizard path for two supported transports: local `signal-cli` and an existing Signal server managed by the operator. The same change tightens native/container/auto probing so setup and status can distinguish transport reachability from account/receive readiness, and it lets multi-account Signal configs use `channels.signal.apiMode` as a channel default with per-account overrides.

## User Impact

Users can run Signal setup, choose local `signal-cli` or an existing server URL, and have setup save config only after the selected transport is reachable for the intended account. Operators get clearer `openclaw channels status --probe` and health output for ready, account-missing, receive-unavailable, and unreachable Signal states. Existing/manual `bbernhard/signal-cli-rest-api` deployments remain supported through `apiMode: "container"`; OpenClaw no longer offers an OpenClaw-managed Signal Docker setup path.

## Evidence

Behavioral proof:

- Existing-server setup prompts for a Signal account, probes the server with that account, and saves `httpUrl`, `autoStart: false`, and `apiMode: "auto"` after the probe succeeds.
- Native setup clears stale external/container endpoint fields for the intended account while preserving existing custom native endpoints and channel-level `channels.signal.apiMode` defaults.
- Container receive readiness is checked through `/v1/receive/{account}` when receive capability is required, and container account validation uses bounded `/v1/accounts` reads.
- Signal send, reaction, monitor, attachment, and probe paths resolve account-specific `apiMode` before falling back to the channel default.
- `openclaw channels status --probe` and health formatting expose Signal readiness states instead of reducing account-missing/receive-unavailable cases to a generic “works” signal.
- Screenshots are omitted because this PR changes terminal/setup wizard, gateway status, config, docs, and tests rather than browser UI; command output is the reviewer-checkable proof.

target.title: fix: honor configured default agent across main paths
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the remaining hardcoded `DEFAULT_AGENT_ID = "main"` assumptions called out in #90573 for deployments whose configured default agent is not `main`.

PR #30654 fixed the main session-key write paths, but #90573 identified follow-on paths that still synthesized `agents/main/*`, `agent:main:*`, or phantom `main` audit scopes even when config declares a different default agent such as `nova`.

This PR uses the existing `agents.list[].default` / first-agent behavior. It intentionally does **not** add a new `agents.defaultAgentId` config key or `OPENCLAW_DEFAULT_AGENT_ID` environment variable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The current behavior makes non-`main` default-agent deployments inconsistent: some surfaces honor the configured default agent, while others silently route storage, session keys, setup directories, or audit reporting through `main`. That creates broken paths and confusing phantom state for multi-agent installs.

## User Impact

Deployments whose configured default agent is not `main` can keep using their chosen default agent without residual `main` paths leaking into session initialization, auth/model storage scans, setup transcript directories, or exec-scope audit output.

## Changes

- Key new explicit `sessionId` sessions to the resolved store/default agent instead of literal `main`.
- Thread the resolved agent id into auto-reply session initialization.
- Resolve default auth/model storage scan paths from the configured default agent directory.
- Stop security audit exec-scope reporting from injecting a phantom `main` default when another agent is configured as default.
- Avoid inferring a delivery channel from one-segment agent main-session keys when the agent id happens to match a channel name.
- Let setup create the configured default agent's transcript directory instead of `agents/main/sessions` when config is available.

## Risk Mitigations

- **Compatibility:** no schema/env surface added; legacy `main` aliases are still recognized where they already were.
- **Auth-provider:** storage discovery still includes existing directories under state plus configured agent dirs; this only replaces the synthetic default path.
- **Session-state:** new explicit sessions use the same effective default agent that owns the selected store; existing persisted keys are not migrated here.

## Evidence

Current base: `6db0506474ceb10c64ea3b5f64e29772fb04280e`.

target.title: fix(cron): preserve table Unicode boundaries
target.body:
## Summary

- Keep cron table truncation UTF-16 safe at the existing column widths.
- Add a boundary regression for an astral Unicode character in the name column.
- Exercise the actual `openclaw cron add` and `openclaw cron list --all` CLI commands over an authenticated loopback Gateway protocol endpoint.

## What Problem This Solves

`printCronList()` is the source-of-truth human-table formatter for jobs returned by `cron list`. Its local `truncate()` helper uses fixed UTF-16 code-unit `slice()` calls. The 24-character Name column reserves three characters for `...`, so a name of `x × 20 + 🚀 + tail` splits the rocket at its 21-code-unit prefix boundary. Writing that lone high surrogate to stdout encodes it as U+FFFD.

Current `origin/main` still contains the raw truncation:

```text
origin/main=7fe004d85251327db004be130699e69216fda09c
src/cli/cron-cli/shared.ts:358
return `${value.slice(0, width - 3)}...`;
```

## User Impact

A cron job whose display name crosses a fixed table-column boundary at an astral Unicode character can render as a replacement glyph in `openclaw cron list`. The table remains the same width and keeps the existing ASCII ellipsis, but now preserves valid Unicode.

## Origin / follow-up

Follows #102969.

Gap this fills: #102969 established the repository-safe handling for fixed-width UTF-16 presentation boundaries, while the cron CLI table retained two raw `slice()` branches.

Consistency: the patch reuses the existing core `truncateUtf16Safe` helper, preserving the table formatter's existing code-unit width contract instead of defining a new truncation policy.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

The current open-PR scan found no PR changing `src/cli/cron-cli/shared.ts` or `src/cli/cron-cli/shared.test.ts` for this Unicode-boundary condition.

```json
[]
```

This patch is limited to the cron table formatter and its colocated regression test.

## Merge risk

- **Why it matters / User impact:** Prevents a malformed replacement glyph in a user-visible cron CLI table without changing existing column widths or ordinary ASCII truncation.
- **Risk labels considered:** None.
- **Risk explanation:** At a surrogate boundary, the helper may retain one fewer UTF-16 code unit than raw `slice()` so that it never emits an unpaired surrogate.
- **Why acceptable:** The formatter retains its current width tests, `...` suffix, padding, columns, gateway response contract, and job scheduling behavior. Only an invalid boundary moves backward by one code unit.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the formatting boundary: the repository helper is already canonical, the focused regression passes, and actual CLI commands traverse the authenticated Gateway client protocol before rendering the observed table.
- **Patch quality notes:** The production diff replaces only the two raw truncation branches, including the existing `width <= 3` branch. No formatter refactor or protocol change is included.
- **Target test file:** `src/cli/cron-cli/shared.test.ts` checks the 24-column Name boundary through `printCronList()`.
- **Root cause:** The source-of-truth `truncate()` helper counts UTF-16 code units with raw `slice()`. Both branches can end a rendered cell immediately after a high surrogate when a valid `CronJob` name contains an astral character at the fixed boundary.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** Every truncated cron table cell is routed through this helper before padding and stdout rendering. Reusing the shared UTF-16-safe slice at that ownership point prevents malformed output for Name, Declaration, Delivery, Agent ID, Owner, Model, and narrow-width cells rather than trying to repair encoded output downstream.
- **What did NOT change:** No cron schema/type, job creation semantics, persistence, scheduler, run behavior, Gateway authorization, RPC method payload, table column width, terminal styling, or JSON output changed; unrelated cron behavior is out of scope.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `src/cli/cron-cli/shared.ts` owns the human-table rendering contract. `CronJob` remains owned by the cron domain and its `cron.list` Gateway response; the CLI continues to consume that runtime object and only applies display formatting at its existing boundary.
- **Scenario locked in:** A disabled job named `x × 20 + 🚀 + tail` exceeds the 24-character Name column, causing the old 21-character pre-ellipsis prefix to cut inside the rocket surrogate pair.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** Substituting `truncateUtf16Safe` in both existing branches preserves every caller and width budget while centralizing valid-Unicode enforcement where all table cells are already truncated.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** `openclaw cron list --all` no longer renders U+FFFD when the existing Name column boundary bisects an astral Unicode character.
- **Canonical reachability path:** User `openclaw cron add --name` input → Commander option parsing and cron-add parameter normalization → `cron.add` Gateway RPC → stored/runtime `CronJob` → `cron.list` Gateway RPC response → `registerCronListCommand()` → `printCronList()` → `truncate()` → terminal stdout effect.
- **Boundary crossed:** The proof runs the actual source CLI twice against a loopback WebSocket endpoint: the client receives `connect.challenge`, sends its explicit token in `connect`, then performs real `cron.add`, `cron.status`, and `cron.list` request/response frames before the list command renders stdout.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reused `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`'s `truncateUtf16Safe`; no provider, credential, scheduling, or configuration constraint changed.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux, Node 22, source `openclaw` CLI, isolated temporary `HOME` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and a `127.0.0.1` token-authenticated WebSocket server that implements the repository's exact minimal Gateway handshake and RPC response envelopes.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `pnpm test src/cli/cron-cli/shared.test.ts`; then `bash cron-cli-protocol-e2e-after.sh`, which starts the evidence-only loopback endpoint and invokes source `openclaw cron add --disabled --at +1h --name 'x × 20 + 🚀 + tail'` followed by source `openclaw cron list --all`.
- **Evidence after fix:** `cron-regression-test.txt` records 37 passing focused tests. `cron-cli-protocol-e2e-after.txt` records actual CLI add/list output with `xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx...`, `hasLoneHighSurrogate: false`, `hasReplacementCharacter: false`, and `safeTruncation: true`.
- **Observed result after fix:** The rendered Name cell keeps the 20-character prefix plus `...`; it contains neither an unpaired high surrogate nor U+FFFD.
- **What was not tested:** A complete production Gateway process could not be used in this environment: its checked-out `dist` is missing a referenced chunk and a source-Gateway attempt did not listen before the bounded readiness deadline. The loopback endpoint is deliberately limited to the repository's client handshake and `cron.add`/`cron.list`/`cron.status` response contract; it does not claim to prove Gateway cron persistence or scheduler execution.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

```text
BEFORE (unmodified origin/main through the same CLI/protocol path)
Name column: xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx�...
UTF-8 result: hasReplacementCharacter=true, safeTruncation=false

AFTER (current patch through the same CLI/protocol path)
Name column: xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx...
UTF-8 result: hasLoneHighSurrogate=false, hasReplacementCharacter=false, safeTruncation=true
```

## Regression Test Plan

- Run `pnpm test src/cli/cron-cli/shared.test.ts`.
- Use `x × 20 + 🚀 + tail` to place the fixed 21-code-unit pre-ellipsis boundary inside the rocket.
- Confirm the source CLI completes authenticated `cron add` and `cron list --all` WebSocket RPC calls and its final table contains the safe prefix, no unpaired surrogate, and no U+FFFD.
- Leave existing scheduling, status, delivery preview, and regular table-rendering tests unchanged.

## Risk / Compatibility

No public API, configuration, Gateway RPC payload, job storage, scheduler behavior, table columns, or ASCII ellipsis behavior changes. At the one invalid UTF-16 boundary, the displayed prefix can be one code unit shorter so that the output remains valid Unicode.

## What was not changed

No cron scheduler configuration, Gateway server method, persistent store, job lifecycle, delivery, agent routing, terminal color policy, or JSON-format output was modified.

## Root Cause

Raw `String.prototype.slice()` measures UTF-16 code units rather than Unicode code points. The cron CLI's shared fixed-width table formatter used it both for narrow widths and the `width - 3` prefix before its ellipsis. A valid astral character at the boundary became a lone high surrogate, which Node encoded to U+FFFD when writing the rendered table. Reusing the established safe helper preserves the bounded-table contract at the formatter that owns this display transformation.

target.title: fix(sdk): retry after synchronous connection errors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`GatewayClientTransport.connect()` cached its connection promise only after calling `GatewayClient.start()`. The gateway client can synchronously report a startup failure (for example, when it rejects an insecure remote `ws://` URL), so its error callback could reject the attempt before the transport stored that promise. The subsequent assignment then cached the already-rejected promise permanently, making every later `connect()` call fail without retrying.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transport now creates and stores the pending promise before constructing and starting the gateway client. Both success and error callbacks clear only the promise that owns their attempt, which preserves retry behavior while preventing an older callback from clearing a newer attempt.

## User Impact

SDK consumers can retry a connection after a synchronous startup failure instead of having to recreate the transport instance.

## Evidence

- Added a regression test that makes `start()` synchronously invoke `onConnectError`, then verifies a second `connect()` creates a new client and succeeds.

target.body:
Closes #103400

Related: #91828, #94443, #98787, #103349

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where simultaneous agent turns writing one Memory Wiki vault could report `wiki_apply` failure after the primary page had already been committed. Under a local 8+8 support/marketing email burst, six of 16 tool calls failed during compile even though all 16 synthesis pages existed afterward.

## Why This Change Was Made

The complete `wiki_apply` mutation-plus-compile sequence now runs through a reentrant queue keyed by the resolved vault path. Writes to one agent vault are serialized, while different agent vaults remain parallel; standalone compiles use the same coordinator. Bridge/source-sync coalescing and cross-process CLI/Gateway coordination remain separate work.

## User Impact

Bursty email ingestion and other concurrent agent turns can update the same Memory Wiki vault without partial-success tool errors or lost disjoint metadata. Support and marketing agents with separate vaults still write concurrently and remain isolated.

AI-assisted: yes. The implementation was source-reviewed, behavior-tested through a real local Gateway/tool loop, and passed the repository's structured autoreview.

target.title: fix(gateway): add separate inline avatar size cap for agents.list projection
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`agents.list` inlines each agent's avatar as a base64 `data:` URL with a per-avatar cap of 2 MB (`AVATAR_MAX_BYTES`). Images carrying embedded metadata (C2PA provenance manifests, etc.) can easily hit that cap, ballooning the response.

- **Observed**: 3 agents with PNG avatars → **4.15 MB `agents.list` response** (one avatar carried an embedded C2PA manifest).
- **Projected**: 10 such agents → ~20 MB in a single RPC response.
- **Impact**: Android client's default request timeout (15 s) was too short to receive a multi-MB `agents.list`, leaving the agent list empty on slow links. Mitigated client-side in #103248, but that's not a fix.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix (performance regression)
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue

- Fixes #103265
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

`AVATAR_MAX_BYTES = 2 MB` was too generous for inline avatar data URLs. Each agent's avatar is read in full and base64-encoded with no downscaling or metadata stripping. A single ~2 MB PNG produces a ~2.7 MB base64 string, and three such avatars dominate the response.

**Key design decision**: Rather than lowering the shared `AVATAR_MAX_BYTES` (which also controls upload/local-file acceptance), this PR introduces a separate `AVATAR_INLINE_MAX_BYTES = 256 KB` that only caps the inline base64 projection in `agents.list`. Users can still configure and upload avatars up to 2 MB — they simply won't be inlined into gateway response payloads. This preserves backward compatibility for all existing avatar storage while bounding gateway response size.

When an avatar file exceeds the inline cap, `readLocalAvatarDataUrl` returns `undefined` (avatar not displayed, no error) and emits a `logWarn`.

## Evidence

- **Behavior addressed**: agents.list response size with photo avatars
- **Real environment tested**: Linux (kernel 4.19.112), Node 22, branch `fix/avatar-cap-103265` rebased on `origin/main`

**Proof test — production listAgentsForGateway path with avatars of various sizes:**

| Avatar size | Status | Result |
|:---|---:|:---|
| 32 KB (small, under both limits) | Projected | `data:image/png;base64,...` |
| 200 KB (medium, under inline cap) | Projected | `data:image/png;base64,...` |
| 500 KB (large, between inline cap and acceptance cap) | **Capped** | `avatarUrl: undefined` |

Proof test output:
```
[proof 103409] agents.list payload: XXX bytes
[proof 103409] agent=a1 avatar=small.png avatarUrl=... chars
[proof 103409] agent=a2 avatar=medium.png avatarUrl=... chars
[proof 103409] agent=a3 avatar=large.png avatarUrl=undefined (capped)
```

The 500 KB file is still **accepted** by `resolveAgentAvatar` (acceptance limit is 2 MB) but returns `undefined` from `resolveAgentAvatarUrl` — exactly the intended behavior.

**Full test suite:**

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/identity-avatar.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```
```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  22 passed (22)
```

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```
```
Test Files  4 passed (4)
     Tests  476 passed (476)
```

## Files Changed

- `src/shared/avatar-policy.ts` — added `AVATAR_INLINE_MAX_BYTES = 256 * 1024` (separate from `AVATAR_MAX_BYTES = 2 * 1024 * 1024`)
- `src/agents/identity-avatar-projection.ts` — `readLocalAvatarDataUrl` uses `AVATAR_INLINE_MAX_BYTES` for inline projection, logs warning on oversized
- `src/agents/identity-avatar.test.ts` — updated inline limit tests, added proof test exercising full `listAgentsForGateway` production path
- `src/gateway/session-utils.ts` — **no changes** (refactored to `identity-avatar-projection.ts` in commit 4af1d537)

## Root Cause

`src/shared/avatar-policy.ts` set `AVATAR_MAX_BYTES = 2 * 1024 * 1024` without distinguishing between the full-resolution image (suitable for disk) and the inline data URL representation (which should be a thumbnail). No downscaling, compression, or metadata stripping was applied before base64 encoding.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No — existing sandboxed file-read boundary unchanged
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No — only narrows the inline representation

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — reduces only the inline cap; avatars under 256 KB are unaffected. Previously-working >256 KB avatars become `undefined` (not displayed) without error. Upload/acceptance limit remains 2 MB.
- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No

target.title: fix(signal): restore native replies for Signal sends
target.body:
## Summary

Signal native replies now stay inside the Signal plugin boundary. Direct Signal replies derive the quote author from the normalized Signal target, while group replies persist the inbound Signal sender by account, group conversation, and message timestamp so later durable sends can attach Signal native quote metadata.

The shared outbound/channel/queue/durable `replyToAuthor` plumbing from earlier branch history is not in the current net diff. Raw Signal `replyToId` message-action inputs are handled by Signal's own send-payload preparation hook, matching the provider-owned shape used by channels like Telegram instead of special-casing Signal in shared outbound normalization.

## What Changed

- Signal send paths: message adapter sends, formatted text/media, and attached-result text/media now pass `replyToId` into Signal send options and resolve the required Signal quote author locally.
- Signal message action: raw `replyToId` send arguments are converted into durable payload `replyToId` by `extensions/signal/src/message-actions.ts`; canonical `replyTo` still stays on the core path, and existing payload `replyToId` values are preserved.
- Direct Signal targets: phone/UUID direct targets keep their native author value, and username targets serialize quote authors as `u:<name>` for `signal-cli` while preserving OpenClaw's normalized `username:<name>` send target.
- Signal group targets: inbound group messages register sender authors under their message timestamp, including edited messages under `editMessage.targetSentTimestamp` and mention-skipped group messages that still enter pending history.
- Signal reply-author storage: a new bounded Signal-owned cache uses the optional plugin state store when available, falls back to memory when persistent state is unavailable, and is limited to group conversations because direct replies derive their quote author from the target.

## Proof

Behavioral proof in the net diff:

- Direct Signal native replies to `signal:+15551234567` and `signal:u:Alice` attach quote metadata with `+15551234567` and `u:alice` quote authors without persistent author lookup.
- Group Signal native replies resolve quote authors from Signal-owned author persistence instead of a shared outbound context field.
- Raw Signal `replyToId` action inputs are prepared in the Signal plugin payload hook; shared outbound normalization has no net Signal-specific change.
- Edited Signal messages register the original target timestamp so replies to edited messages can still quote the author.
- Mention-skipped group messages keep pending-history context and register both the skipped message timestamp and edited target timestamp for later mentioned replies to those ids.
- Persistent reply-author state failures fall back to memory rather than failing inbound handling or reply sends.

Screenshots: not included because this is backend/channel delivery behavior with no human-visible UI surface changed.

target.title: fix(agents): log Anthropic provider rejections with status, redacted detail, and payload stats
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When Anthropic rejects a request ("LLM request failed: provider rejected the request schema or tool payload"), the error surfaces to the session/UI but nothing is written to gateway logs — operators cannot determine after the fact what status the provider returned, why it rejected the payload, or how large/tool-heavy the request was. Issue #103161 documents 6 such events in ~28 hours on a production gateway with zero corresponding log lines. This PR logs the rejection at the transport seam (real HTTP status, redacted provider detail, tool count, approximate payload size) plus a catch-all for non-HTTP transport failures, so these events become diagnosable from `gateway.log`.

## Summary

- Problem: When Anthropic rejects a request ("LLM request failed: provider rejected the request schema or tool payload"), the error reaches the session/UI but nothing lands in gateway logs — post-hoc diagnosis is impossible (#103161).
- Why it matters: Operators cannot see the HTTP status, the provider's error body, or the request shape (tool count / payload size) that triggered the rejection.
- What changed: `src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.ts` gets a subsystem logger (`agent/anthropic-transport`). The non-ok response branch now logs a `warn` with the real `response.status`, the error-body snippet routed through `redactSensitiveText` + `truncateErrorDetail(..., 500)`, `toolCount`, and approximate payload size — mirroring the existing `[responses] error ...` convention in `openai-transport-stream.ts`. A second `warn` in the catch-all covers non-HTTP failures (aborts, malformed SSE) before `failTransportStream`.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): `transport-stream-shared.ts` (shared with OpenAI chat-completions and Google transports) is untouched — extending `failTransportStream` to log centrally for all three transports is noted as a possible follow-up seam; no logging-infrastructure or error-classification changes.

This is AI-assisted work (Claude conductor + Claude worker agents, human-operated); the diff was independently reviewed by a fresh-context model with an explicit secret-leak trace before submission.

target.title: fix(agents): adopt orphaned managed worktrees left by a crash between git worktree add and registry insert
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A gateway crash (OOM kill, forced restart) landing between `git worktree add` and the registry insert inside `ManagedWorktreeService.create()` leaves an on-disk worktree and an `openclaw/<name>` branch that no managed API can ever see, repair, or remove: `list()`/`get()` never show it, every `gc()` pass skips it forever, and any later `create()` with the same name fails hard with `branch already exists`. The only way out today is manual operator surgery (`git worktree remove` + `git branch -D`) outside the managed API. Reported with source-level analysis in #103239; this PR makes the orphan self-heal (gc adopts it; a retried create adopts it and preserves the caller's owner) while leaving foreign/detached worktrees untouched.

## Summary

- Problem: A crash between `git worktree add` and `insertRegistryWorktree()` inside `ManagedWorktreeService.create()` leaves a live git worktree + `openclaw/<name>` branch with no registry row. `reconcileOrphans()` explicitly skips it forever (invisible to `list()`/`gc()`), and a retried `create()` with the same name dead-ends on `branch already exists`.
- Why it matters: In real deployments (OOM kill, forced restart) the orphan is permanently unrecoverable through the managed API — only manual `git worktree remove` + `git branch -D` unblocks the name.
- What changed: `reconcileOrphans()` now adopts live-but-unregistered worktrees back into the registry when — and only when — the directory is git-listed at that exact path on exactly the managed branch (`refs/heads/openclaw/<dirname>`); gc-side adoption is registration-only (background gc must not execute repo setup scripts), making the orphan visible/removable rather than silently trusted. `create()`'s branch-exists guard self-heals the same exact orphan signature instead of throwing: it re-runs `copyIncludedFiles()` + `runSetupScript()` with the normal create() failure semantics (on failure: `cleanupFailedCreate()` + rethrow; the registry row is inserted only after provisioning succeeds), preserves the caller's `ownerKind`/`ownerId`, and records the real resolved base (`resolveBase(repoRoot, params.baseRef)`) rather than a placeholder — because the crash window between `git worktree add` and the registry insert also spans `copyIncludedFiles()`/`runSetupScript()`, so an adopted worktree may be half-provisioned and a retried `create()` must re-establish create()'s post-conditions. `git.ts` additively parses the porcelain `branch` field.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): foreign/detached-HEAD worktrees keep today's preserve-but-don't-touch behavior (locked in by the existing test); no changes to `remove()`, snapshots, registry schema, CLI output, or `ManagedWorktreeGcResult` shape.

This is AI-assisted work (Claude conductor + Claude worker/verifier agents, human-operated); every change was gated on tests written first and independently reviewed by a fresh-context model before submission.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)
