target.title: fix #91171: [Bug]: Sub-agent model routing ignores model parameter, silently falls back to deepseek
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: `sessions_spawn` could report an explicit requested model as applied while the child `agent` gateway launch still omitted provider/model and ran through the default route.
- Solution: forward the resolved provider/model into the child launch only for explicit `sessions_spawn.model`, and authorize that override at the existing gateway boundary.
- What changed: `spawnSubagentDirect` now adds provider/model to the initial child `agent` request for explicit model overrides; in-process gateway dispatch can merge internal `allowModelOverride` into the scoped client so plugin/run metadata is preserved.
- What did NOT change: no new config/schema/protocol fields; no model catalog/default policy change; no-explicit-model sub-agent spawns do not forward provider/model as explicit gateway overrides.
- Why it matters / User impact: users spawning a sub-agent for a model-specific task, such as image-capable Qwen from a default DeepSeek session, need the actual child run to use that requested model instead of silently falling back to a model without the needed capabilities.
- Branch history note: this branch was rebased onto the current `main` to resolve an unrelated-histories fork base (the fork shared no common ancestor with `origin/main`, producing a 10k-file phantom diff). The two original fix/test commits were cherry-picked onto `main`; the only manual resolution was in `subagent-spawn.ts` where `main` had since upgraded the scope resolver from `isAdminOnlyMethod` to `resolveLeastPrivilegeOperatorScopesForMethod`, so the model-override auth condition is now OR'd into the new resolver while preserving both intents. No behavior change beyond the original fix.
- Fixes #91171

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Explicit `sessions_spawn.model` was resolved and reported but not passed to the child gateway `agent` request that starts the actual sub-agent run.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw source checkout on Windows Git Bash, using Node 22.19.0 from npm `node@22.19.0`, an isolated loopback OpenClaw gateway, and a configured Claude CLI backend for `claude-cli/claude-sonnet-4-6`; focused Vitest used the repository `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` wrapper.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Live proof: started a local loopback gateway with isolated config/state and invoked `spawnSubagentDirect({ model: "claude-cli/claude-sonnet-4-6", mode: "run", cleanup: "keep" })` against that gateway; then read gateway `status` for the spawned child session. Regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/subagent-spawn.test.ts src/gateway/server-plugins.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.subagents.sessions-spawn.model.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts`; `git diff --check`.
- **Evidence after fix:** The live spawn returned `status: "accepted"`, `resolvedProvider: "claude-cli"`, `resolvedModel: "claude-cli/claude-sonnet-4-6"`, and `modelApplied: true` for child session `agent:dev:subagent:086240a8-3915-42ab-97e4-41b84c29704e`; a follow-up gateway `status` row for that child showed `kind: "spawn-child"`, `configuredModel: "claude-cli/claude-sonnet-4-6"`, `selectedModel: "claude-cli/claude-sonnet-4-6"`, and `runtime: "Claude CLI"`.
- **Post-rebase regression on current `main` base:** After rebasing onto `main` (`ee1450d6`), `vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/subagent-spawn.test.ts` → 25/26 passed (the one failure, `keeps spawn cwd separate from inherited agent workspace`, is a Windows POSIX-path mismatch `E:\tmp\task-repo` vs expected `/tmp/task-repo`, unrelated to this fix and reproducible on `main`); `vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/server-plugins.test.ts` → 59/59 passed. The model-override assertions (`allowInternalModelOverride`, admin-scope pinning for out-of-process override auth) all pass on the new base.
- **Observed result after fix:** A real local spawned child run selected the same explicit provider/model that `sessions_spawn`/`spawnSubagentDirect` resolved, instead of falling back to the default route. Tests additionally assert that explicit `sessions_spawn.model: "openai/gpt-5.4"` produces child `agent` params with `provider: "openai"` and `model: "gpt-5.4"`; in-process explicit `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` dispatch forwards provider/model with internal override authorization; no-explicit-model spawn asserts provider/model remain undefined.
- **What was not tested:** The reporter's exact live QQ/Qwen/DeepSeek channel setup was not run. The live proof uses a local Claude CLI provider/model available in this environment, exercising the same gateway launch boundary identified in the issue: whether the requested provider/model is selected by the spawned child run.

## Review findings addressed

- **RF-001:** Addressed for the current author-action label by pushing the CI assertion repair and keeping the proof/maintainer-risk disclosures in this body for re-review.
- **RF-002:** Fixed the failing sub-agent test assertions: the no-explicit-model in-process path now expects no internal override option, and the explicit in-process model test checks the actual dispatch params/options without requiring absent fields as own `undefined` properties. Reran the focused subagent/gateway regression command successfully.
- **RF-003:** Disclosed in `Merge risk`: the WebSocket path uses admin scope only when an explicit provider/model override needs gateway authorization; in-process dispatch merges internal `allowModelOverride` into the scoped client instead of forcing a synthetic admin client. This auth-provider boundary remains called out for maintainer acceptance.
- **RF-004:** Disclosed: the reporter's exact QQ/Qwen/DeepSeek setup was not rerun. The live proof uses a local Claude CLI provider/model while exercising the same child gateway launch boundary and selected-model status evidence.
- **RF-005:** Addressed with a narrow automated test repair only; no product direction or production routing behavior was changed in the follow-up.
- **RF-006:** Fixed `src/agents/subagent-spawn.test.ts:362-400` dispatch option expectations as described in RF-002.
- **RF-007:** Verified with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/subagent-spawn.test.ts src/gateway/server-plugins.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.subagents.sessions-spawn.model.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts` after the test repair; exit 0.
- **RF-008:** Verified with `git diff --check` after the test repair; exit 0.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/agents/subagent-spawn.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-plugins.test.ts`, `src/agents/openclaw-tools.subagents.sessions-spawn.model.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** Explicit `sessions_spawn.model` forwards resolved provider/model to the child launch; in-process override authorization preserves scoped client metadata; no-explicit-model spawns do not become explicit provider/model overrides.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The tests assert the exact gateway `agent` request shape at the seam that starts the child run, avoiding live-provider flakiness while proving the routing data the gateway handler consumes.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** auth-provider, security-boundary, session-state, message-delivery, availability, compatibility, automation.
- **Risk explanation:** The change touches provider/model routing and gateway authorization for sub-agent launches. The public contract risk is limited to the existing `sessions_spawn.model` parameter; related open PRs were scanned by the daily-fix flow and treated as advisory background, not blockers. Message delivery/session fields are only moved in formatting around the same `agent` request object, not semantically changed.
- **Why acceptable:** Forwarding is gated on an explicit `sessions_spawn.model` value, so automatic/default model resolution is not converted into a gateway override. In-process authorization merges `allowModelOverride` into the scoped client instead of forcing a synthetic admin client, preserving plugin/run metadata. Regression tests cover explicit and no-explicit-model paths.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** `spawnSubagentDirect` resolved `params.model` and persisted the resolved provider/model into the child session, but the subsequent gateway `agent` call that starts the child run did not include that resolved `provider`/`model`; the gateway handler can only honor explicit model routing from request fields it receives.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The patch changes the source-of-truth launch request before the child model is selected, rather than relying on status metadata or downstream fallback after the wrong route is chosen.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High: source-level regression tests cover the request shape, and local live gateway proof shows an explicit provider/model selected by the spawned child run. The only remaining proof gap is the reporter's exact QQ/Qwen/DeepSeek setup.
- **Patch quality notes:** Focused production diff plus regression tests. The timeout field appears in the patch only because the `agent` request object was wrapped to pass authorization options; the value and timeout behavior are unchanged. No guard/catch/default workaround or lockfile change.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** Owner boundary is `spawnSubagentDirect` constructing the child gateway `agent` request and `dispatchGatewayMethodInProcessRaw` selecting the gateway client metadata. This changes routing data before gateway model selection; it does not alter mirrored session status alone, public schema, or downstream provider fallback policy.

target.title: fix #95295: [Bug]: Web UI sidebar hides existing child-spawned subagent sessions across agent scopes
target.body:
Fixes #95295.

## What Problem This Solves

- **Affected surface / workflow:** Control UI sidebar session discovery across configured agent scopes.
- **Root cause, in product terms:** The default sidebar request is intentionally scoped to the selected agent, and the sidebar projection independently removes subagent-keyed and `spawnedBy` rows. The prior opt-in implementation widened both layers through shared session state, so a later scoped chat refresh could replace the all-agent rows while the **All agents** button remained pressed.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** Persisted child-spawned work could exist in another agent store but remain undiscoverable from the sidebar, and the previous toggle could visibly claim an all-agent view while showing only one agent's sessions.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Fix classification:** Root-cause repair.
- **Complete shipped solution:** The default sidebar remains scoped. Pressing **All agents** performs the existing unscoped `sessions.list({})` request into sidebar-owned state, enables child/spawned rows only for that local result, and leaves shared canonical scoped state untouched. Canonical list revisions and session-created events coalesce background refreshes of the local result; stale responses, disconnects, gateway-client replacement, and session-capability replacement cannot reactivate old rows.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The sidebar now owns both sides of the opt-in invariant: its unscoped data source and its child-row projection. A scoped refresh can continue publishing canonical state without contradicting the pressed control, and disabling the control immediately returns to the latest canonical scoped result.
- **Key design boundary / source of truth:** The existing `sessions.list` contract and combined session-store loader remain authoritative. Omitting `agentId` is already the canonical all-agent read; this patch does not add a protocol, schema, config, persistence, or migration contract.
- **Non-goals / what did not change:** The Sessions page, command palette, primary-session selection, chat picker, default scoped visibility, gateway protocol/schema, persisted transcript format, and session migration behavior are unchanged.
- **Compatibility, merge-risk, or maintainer-decision notes:** The behavior is default-off and sidebar-only. Maintainers should still confirm that opt-in sidebar discovery of persisted child transcripts across configured agents is the intended product boundary.
- **Risk labels considered:** `merge-risk: session-state`, visibility boundary, compatibility, and performance.
- **Risk explanation:** The opt-in mode can reveal persisted child/subagent transcripts from other configured agent scopes and performs a bounded all-agent list read. It does not mutate shared canonical state or stored sessions.
- **Why acceptable:** The wider visibility is explicit and user initiated; archived, global, unknown, and cron rows remain excluded; the existing list limit/configured-agent behavior remains in force; and default behavior is unchanged.
- **Patch quality notes:** Production changes are confined to sidebar state/rendering, the existing navigation projection, and the scope-control style. The additional E2E change is the requested visible-browser regression. No suppression directives, skipped tests, lockfile changes, protocol changes, or unrelated refactors were added.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for contributor-side correctness and the current-main port; final cross-agent transcript visibility scope remains an explicit maintainer product decision.

## User Impact

- **Users/operators/developers can now:** Enable **All agents** in the sidebar and rediscover an existing cross-agent child-spawned session, while newly created sessions and canonical list revisions refresh that opt-in view.
- **Existing behavior preserved:** With the control off, the sidebar remains agent-scoped and continues hiding subagent-keyed and `spawnedBy` rows. Scoped chat/session refreshes continue publishing their normal canonical result.
- **What was not tested or remains unavailable:** This repair did not rerun a long-lived provider-backed gateway with real user transcripts. The PR already has reviewer-viewable gateway/store/browser proof and carries `proof: sufficient`; the fresh repair adds a current-main Chromium mocked-Gateway E2E and captured local screenshot rather than claiming a new live-provider run.

## Evidence

- **Environment:** Windows Git Bash, Node `v22.17.0`, pnpm `11.2.2`, repository Playwright Chromium, current `origin/main`. pnpm reported the repository's preferred Node floor (`>=22.19.0`) as a non-fatal warning.
- **Commands run after this patch:**
  - `pnpm test ui/src/lib/sessions/navigation.test.ts ui/src/components/app-sidebar.test.ts`
  - `OPENCLAW_CAPTURE_UI_PROOF=1 pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts ui/src/e2e/session-management.e2e.test.ts`
  - `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`
  - `pnpm ui:i18n:check`
  - `pnpm ui:build`
  - `pnpm exec oxfmt --check ui/src/components/app-sidebar.ts ui/src/components/app-sidebar.test.ts ui/src/lib/sessions/navigation.ts ui/src/lib/sessions/navigation.test.ts ui/src/styles/layout.css ui/src/e2e/session-management.e2e.test.ts`
  - `git diff --check`
- **Key results / observations:** Focused UI tests passed 2 files / 23 tests. The Chromium E2E passed 1 file / 10 tests; its new scenario locates scoped `Main`, verifies the cross-agent child is absent, presses **All agents**, locates `Subagent: Planner`, verifies `aria-pressed="true"`, and verifies the final `sessions.list` request omits `agentId`. UI test type-check, all 20 locale checks, production Control UI build, formatting, and diff whitespace checks passed. Public existing proof: [Real behavior proof run 29063489211 / job 86270110876](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29063489211/job/86270110876); the PR carries `proof: sufficient`. A full repository type-check attempt encountered an unrelated current-main `TS4058` in `src/secrets/config-io.ts`; this PR does not modify that file, and the requested UI type-check passes.
- **Review findings addressed, if any:** RF-001 contributor work is addressed by the current-main port and fresh requested validation. RF-002, RF-003, and RF-006 are fixed by sidebar-owned all-agent data and tested scoped-refresh isolation. RF-004 and RF-005 are addressed by the focused current-main port. RF-007 passed with 23 focused tests. RF-008 passed with 10 Chromium E2E tests including the cross-agent child reveal. RF-009 passed (`pnpm tsgo:test:ui`). RF-010 passed (`pnpm ui:i18n:check`, all locales clean). RF-011 passed (`git diff --check`). Product acceptance of the default-off visibility boundary remains a maintainer decision.
- **Regression guardrail:** Navigation tests lock down scoped/default filtering and all-agent exclusions; component tests lock down local request ownership, scoped-refresh isolation, revision/created-event refreshes, in-flight coalescing, stale-response rejection, lifecycle resets, and failure fallback; the Chromium E2E locks down the rendered control, visible child locator, and omitted `agentId` request.

target.body:
> [!NOTE]
> **AI-Assisted Contribution:** This PR was prepared and validated with the assistance of an AI coding assistant (Antigravity/Gemini).

## What Problem This Solves
Resolves a problem where the model auth subsystem ignores explicit `apiKey` (literal or SecretRef) overrides in `models.json` if store profiles exist (pr #100839).

**Symptom/Behavior:**
1. Unless `auth: "api-key"` is explicitly set (making `shouldPreferExplicitConfigApiKeyAuth` true), the literal key or SecretRef configured in `models.json` is ignored during the binding phase (falling through `providerEntryBinding` checks). The function then scans the profile store; if any profile is found for the provider, it overrides the user's explicit `apiKey` configuration.
2. Additionally, when a specific profile was requested (e.g. during failover rotation or pinned session), the early check for explicit models.json `apiKey` would bypass profile resolution entirely and return the models.json `apiKey` instead of the rotated profile, causing E2E failover tests (`rotates for overloaded assistant failures across auto-pinned profiles`) to fail.
3. In `models status` and `models auth list` commands, placeholder/marker values in the environment (e.g. `GOOGLE_API_KEY`) were treated as literal keys, causing incorrect `effective=models.json` formatting instead of falling back to store profiles.

Affected locations:
- [resolveApiKeyForProvider](file:///home/dietpi/Developer/openclaw/src/agents/model-auth.ts#L1071-L1084)
- [resolveProviderAuthOverview](file:///home/dietpi/Developer/openclaw/src/commands/models/list.auth-overview.ts#L152-L163)

3. Updated `resolveUsableCustomProviderApiKey` in `src/agents/model-auth.ts` to correctly filter out environment-resolved placeholder markers.

---

target.title: fix(inworld): add timeout to voices list request
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Inworld voice discovery could wait indefinitely when the voices endpoint accepted the HTTP connection but never returned a response.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Inworld TTS paths already receive bounded provider timeouts, but `listInworldVoices` did not apply a deadline to its guarded voices-list request. The provider hook calls `listInworldVoices` without passing `timeoutMs`, so the request was falling through to the underlying unbounded fetch.

This change adds a bounded default timeout for voice discovery while preserving existing request headers, SSRF policy, and response parsing. Callers that pass an explicit `timeoutMs` continue to have it honored.

## User Impact

A stalled Inworld voices endpoint no longer blocks voice discovery forever. The discovery request now fails boundedly instead of leaving callers pending.

## Evidence

- Added mock-based regression tests in `extensions/inworld/tts.test.ts` verifying default `timeoutMs: 30_000` and explicit timeout preservation.
- Added live timeout proof in `extensions/inworld/voices-timeout.test.ts` using a local `node:http` loopback server that accepts the connection but never responds; the test stubs `globalThis.fetch` to redirect the guarded request to `127.0.0.1` and asserts `listInworldVoices({ ..., timeoutMs: 250 })` rejects with an abort/timeout error within 2 seconds.
- Ran `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run extensions/inworld/` — `Test Files  3 passed (3)`, `Tests  42 passed (42)`.

target.title: fix(gateway): cap pendingFinalDelivery retries and prevent delivery wedge
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A gateway restart while a final reply was pending could wedge that delivery forever. Restart recovery replayed stale `pendingFinalDelivery` payloads with no cap and no backoff, and a payload that a downstream route never cleared was replayed on every subsequent restart. This PR bounds that recovery:

- Recent attempts back off exponentially (30s base, 30 min ceiling) and payloads are dead-lettered after 10 recovery attempts by default, clearing the pending-final and restart-recovery fields so the session no longer stays restart-recoverable forever.
- Future persisted `pendingFinalDeliveryLastAttemptAt` values are treated as no active backoff, so clock skew, VM resume, or NTP correction cannot preserve the wedge.
- Backoff-deferred entries are surfaced from `recoverStore` as a closed `deferred` shape (count plus earliest `nextEligibleAtMs`), and the startup scheduler runs one bounded follow-up recovery pass when the earliest backoff expires. This addresses the ClawSweeper P1: previously a backoff-active entry only counted as skipped and the scheduler re-queued only on `failed > 0`, so the entry waited for the next gateway restart. Follow-up passes do not consume the failed-retry budget and are naturally bounded by the per-entry attempt cap (dead-letter) and the backoff ceiling.
- The cap is threaded through the restart recovery entry points so tests and callers can tune it.

## Context

This follows up on #92082 and the July 5, 2026 restart incident where pending final delivery state was part of the delivery wedge investigation. Current `main` already carries the v2026.6.5 fixes for bounded heartbeat scheduling and preserved delivery context; this patch closes the remaining startup-recovery path that could keep replaying a durable pending final across gateway restarts.

The Telegram ingress fixes requested alongside this work (#93281, #96962, #97118) are already ancestors of current `main`, so there was no scoped upstream backport diff to open for that part.

## Evidence

All commands run on `37fb71f5b07067f4023527a8d3e3667f9bd155c8` (rebased on current `main` 827f2c44225e):

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts` — 1 file, 38 tests passed, including the new scheduler-level regression: a pending final inside backoff is retried after expiry without a restart (fake timers drive the scheduler; the resume fires only after the 60s attempt-2 backoff elapses).
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.ts src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts` — all files correctly formatted.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.ts src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts` — clean.
- `git diff --check` — clean.
- `pnpm build` — full build green (tsdown + postbuild + plugin assets).

Live restart-recovery proof, re-run after the scheduler fix: an isolated Node process imported the rebuilt `dist` recovery module with a temp `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and a localhost-only minimal fake gateway (connect challenge + hello-ok + `agent` acceptor). Seeded one pending final at `attemptCount=1` with `lastAttemptAt` 25s old (30s backoff, eligible in ~5s), then called `scheduleRestartAbortedMainSessionRecovery`. The production gateway was not restarted or contacted. Redacted output:

```text
PROOF phase=schedule start attemptCount=1 lastAttemptAt=25s-old backoff=30s eligibleIn~5s port=65180
[main-session-restart-recovery] pending final delivery restart recovery backoff active for agent:main:proof-pending-final after 1/10 attempts
PROOF phase=deferred result acceptedAgentRequests=0 persistedAttemptCount=1 abortedLastRun=true
PROOF fake-gateway accepted agent request #1
[main-session-restart-recovery] resumed interrupted main session: agent:main:proof-pending-final (with pending payload)
[main-session-restart-recovery] main-session restart recovery complete: recovered=1 failed=0 skipped=0
PROOF phase=follow-up result acceptedAgentRequests=1 persistedAttemptCount=2 abortedLastRun=false pendingFinalDelivery=true
PROOF verdict=PASS
```

The deferred entry was not retried by the first pass, and the scheduler's follow-up pass retried it in-process once the backoff expired: attempt count 1 -> 2, `abortedLastRun` cleared, exactly one `agent` request accepted.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: a pending final delivery inside its restart-recovery backoff window was never retried in the same process because the startup scheduler only re-queued failed passes; it stayed wedged until the next gateway restart.
- Real environment tested: macOS (Darwin 25.5.0), Node 26.4.0, isolated Node process driving the rebuilt `dist` recovery module from this branch with a temp state dir and a localhost-only fake gateway; no production gateway involved.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: seeded `sessions.json` with `pendingFinalDelivery=true`, `pendingFinalDeliveryAttemptCount=1`, `pendingFinalDeliveryLastAttemptAt` 25s old; ran `scheduleRestartAbortedMainSessionRecovery({ stateDir, delayMs: 200 })` from `dist/main-session-restart-recovery-*.js`; also ran `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts`.
- Evidence after fix: redacted live output above (`PROOF verdict=PASS`) plus vitest `Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 38 passed (38)`.
- Observed result after fix: first recovery pass deferred the backoff-active entry without calling the gateway; the scheduled follow-up pass fired after backoff expiry, the fake gateway accepted exactly one `agent` retry, and the store showed `pendingFinalDeliveryAttemptCount` 1 -> 2 with `abortedLastRun=false`.
- What was not tested: live gateway restart-recovery soak on upstream main.

target.title: fix(sessions): ground assistant transcript media refs before replay
target.body:
## Summary

Grounds assistant transcript text before session-context replay: an absolute path under the managed media dir that does not resolve to a real file is redacted to `[unverified media reference removed]`, keeping the surrounding prose. User text is never rewritten, and paths outside the managed media dir (code paths, host paths) are exempt so ordinary technical conversation is untouched.

Motivation is a live incident on a production gateway (2026-07-06): a bare 3-character inbound message ("Hey", no attachment, WhatsApp plugin disabled) produced an assistant turn containing `IMAGE:<media-dir>/whats-app-image-2026-07-06-...jpg` plus a detailed description of an image that never existed on disk or in the gateway inbound log. The session-context replay then compiled that fabricated text into every subsequent prompt (`context.compiled` / `prompt.submitted` in the trajectory), making the hallucination self-reinforcing for the rest of the session.

The invariant this leans on: legitimate inbound media never reaches prompts as a raw absolute path -- `media-note.ts` normalizes managed refs to `media://inbound/...`. So a raw absolute managed-media path inside *assistant* text is either fabricated or expired; both are unusable and safe to redact. This deliberately does not attempt free-text hallucination detection -- it only removes verifiably ungrounded media references, deterministically, with zero model calls.

Implementation: `redactUngroundedMediaRefs` in `src/config/sessions/transcript-grounding.ts`, wired into `parseRecentConversationText` (assistant branch only) in `src/config/sessions/transcript.ts`, which serves `readRecentUserAssistantTextForSession` and its plugin-sdk consumers (e.g. the Telegram session transcript context). Handles the macOS `/private/var` twin, path-token boundaries (no substring matches inside longer paths or words), and trailing sentence punctuation; returns the same reference on no-op.

## Verification

- New colocated tests: 8 unit cases (fabricated ref redacted with prose kept, verified ref preserved, non-media absolute paths untouched, `/private` twin, token boundaries, trailing punctuation, mixed refs, no-op identity) plus a reader-level regression that replays the observed incident shape through `readRecentUserAssistantTextFromSessionTranscript` against real files in a temp `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` (fabricated ref redacted; real-file ref and user text preserved verbatim).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/transcript-grounding.test.ts src/config/sessions/transcript.test.ts`: 61 passed / 0 failed on this branch (includes the pre-existing 51 transcript reader tests, unchanged).
- `pnpm tsgo:core` clean; `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` clean on touched files.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: A hallucinated managed-media path in an assistant turn (fabricated `IMAGE:<media-dir>/...jpg` reference to a file that never existed) was replayed verbatim into subsequent prompt context, reinforcing the fabrication across the session.
Real environment tested: macOS 26 source checkout; reader-level regression executes the real transcript reader against a real on-disk session transcript and real files under a temp `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` media dir (no mocks in the replay path); incident evidence from a production macOS gateway trajectory (session ab2e822c, 2026-07-06 09:21 EDT).
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/transcript-grounding.test.ts src/config/sessions/transcript.test.ts`
Evidence after fix: assistant entry text returned by `readRecentUserAssistantTextFromSessionTranscript` is `IMAGE:[unverified media reference removed] That's a serious setup. Original at <real file>.` -- the fabricated path is gone, the verified real-file ref and all prose survive, and the user entry containing the same fake path is returned unmodified.
Observed result after fix: 61 passed / 0 failed.
What was not tested: a live gateway restart/deploy with the incident session replayed end-to-end over Telegram; the fix is currently soaking on a fork deployment branch before fleet rollout.

target.title: refactor(qa): share Matrix flows across channel drivers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QA Lab scenarios could select only one channel driver, which forced Matrix behavior to be duplicated when the same scenario needed both the live Matrix adapter and Crabline's Matrix provider bridge.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add the small shared foundation needed for stacked Matrix QA migration work:

- allow a QA Lab flow to declare multiple supported channel drivers while still requiring the selected channel to match;
- map portable QA actor and conversation identifiers onto Crabline's Matrix endpoint without moving Matrix behavior into the QA adapter;
- run the existing shared/per-room Matrix DM scenarios through either `--channel-driver crabline` or `--channel-driver live` using the normal QA Lab flow host;
- keep coverage-report commands runnable by selecting a concrete supported driver.

This is stack PR 1 of 4. It does not migrate the legacy Matrix scenario/profile catalog, switch release workflows, or remove `qa-matrix`. Those changes remain in stacked successors so this foundation can be reviewed independently.

## User Impact

No shipped Matrix channel behavior changes. QA maintainers can execute the same two Matrix DM session scenarios against Crabline or the live Matrix adapter without adding a Matrix-specific scenario executor.

target.title: [codex] fix gateway restart-required reload drift
target.body:
## Summary

Read-only runtime-config drift diagnostics for gateway health. `openclaw health` (JSON and text) now reports when the running gateway's live config has drifted from the disk file on restart-required paths (model/provider/auth), so an operator can see that a disk-side repair or rotation is waiting on a restart instead of trusting a green health snapshot.

- Adds a `runtimeConfig` block to the health summary: `state: "ok" | "drift" | "unknown"`, live/disk `agents.defaults.model` labels, and the list of drifted paths (tracked: `agents.defaults.model`, `agents.defaults.models`, `agents.list`, `models`, `gateway.auth`, `auth.profiles`, `auth.order`, `secrets.providers`).
- Distinguishes unreadable/missing/invalid disk config (`state: "unknown"` with a generic message for non-admin callers) from real drift, and renders both drift and unknown states in text output.
- Gates config fingerprints (`liveSourceFingerprint`, `diskSourceFingerprint`) and the detailed disk-read error (which can contain the local config path or a parse-error excerpt) to admin-scoped (`operator.admin`) callers.
- Recomputes the drift summary on gateway health cache hits inside `mergeCachedHealthRuntimeState`, mirroring the existing delivery-queue / hot-reload-status recompute pattern, so read-scoped callers always see fresh drift state.

This PR is observability only. The hot-mode restart-required reload behavior change (honoring the restart plan instead of warn-and-keep) is intentionally NOT in this diff; it lives in the companion PR #89517 so behavior and diagnostics can be reviewed and landed independently. An earlier revision of this PR carried both concerns; they were split on 2026-06-08.

## What Problem This Solves

When `gateway.reload.mode` is `hot`, restart-required config changes (model/provider/auth) are warn-and-keep: the gateway logs `config reload requires gateway restart; hot mode ignoring (...)` and keeps running on the old pinned runtime config. Nothing user-visible reported that state afterwards: `openclaw health` said everything was ok while the gateway served stale model routing or an old `gateway.auth` token that no longer matched disk. Operators debugging "my config change did nothing" had only a single gateway log line to find.

This revision also resolves the outstanding ClawSweeper P1 on this PR: `openclaw health` connects least-privilege at `operator.read` and is served from the non-sensitive 60s health cache, so a cached "ok" could mask drift that appeared right after the cache was filled. The previous head gated a cache bypass on `operator.admin`, which never fired for the read-scoped CLI. Instead of extending the bypass, the drift summary is now recomputed on every cache hit (scope-aware; fingerprints stay admin-only) and the admin bypass was deleted -- no cache bypass remains.

## Evidence

All commands below were run at head `4229b9999d` (this branch rebased onto `upstream/main` at `22376d80e1`) in a worktree on macOS (darwin 25.5.0), Node 24.

Unit/regression tests:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/health.snapshot.test.ts src/commands/health.test.ts
  -> Test Files 2 passed (2), Tests 49 passed (49)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts
  -> Test Files 5 passed (5), Tests 525 passed (525)
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json                      -> clean
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json   -> clean
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <7 changed files>                        -> clean
oxfmt --check <7 changed files>                                      -> clean
```

New tests in this revision (`src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts`):

- `recomputes runtime-config drift on cache hits so read-scoped callers see fresh drift` -- cached "ok" + drift recompute -> `operator.read` cache hit (`{ cached: true }` respond flag asserted) returns `state: "drift"` with no fingerprints.
- `threads the admin scope into the cache-hit drift recompute so fingerprints stay admin-only` -- same cache-hit path with `operator.admin` receives fingerprints; background refresh still runs.
- `drops a stale cached runtime-config summary when the recompute returns none`.

Live behavior proof (redacted, exact head): see the `Real behavior proof` section below -- a sandbox gateway built from this head shows the ok -> drift transition on the plain, non-verbose, read-scoped `openclaw health` path after an external `gateway.auth.token` rotation under `mode: "hot"`.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: plain `openclaw health` (least-privilege `operator.read`, both JSON and text) reports `runtimeConfig.state: "drift"` with `driftPaths: ["gateway.auth"]` after an external `gateway.auth.token` rotation under `gateway.reload.mode: "hot"`, including when the response is served from the 60s health cache; fingerprints are omitted for read-scoped callers.

Real environment tested: sandbox gateway on macOS (darwin 25.5.0), dist built from this branch at head `4229b9999d` content, launched with `node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway --port 28934`, isolated `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`/`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, config: `gateway.mode: "local"`, `gateway.auth: { mode: "token", token: "sandbox-token-OLD" }`, `gateway.reload: { mode: "hot", debounceMs: 100 }`, `agents.defaults.model: "openai/gpt-5.5"`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```
node dist/index.js health --json                 # call 1, fills the health cache
sed -i.bak 's/sandbox-token-OLD/sandbox-token-NEW/' $SANDBOX/openclaw.json
sleep 4
OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN=sandbox-token-OLD node dist/index.js health --json   # call 2, ~40s after call 1
OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN=sandbox-token-OLD node dist/index.js health          # text mode
```

Evidence after fix:

- Call 1 (before rotation): `"runtimeConfig": {"state": "ok", "liveDefaultModel": "openai/gpt-5.5", "diskDefaultModel": "openai/gpt-5.5"}` -- no fingerprint fields on the read-scoped path.
- Gateway reload log after `sed`:
  ```
  [reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (gateway.auth.token)
  [reload] config reload requires gateway restart; hot mode ignoring (gateway.auth.token)
  ```
- Call 2 (after rotation, inside the 60s `HEALTH_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS` window of call 1, i.e. the cache-hit merge path): `"runtimeConfig": {"state": "drift", "liveDefaultModel": "openai/gpt-5.5", "diskDefaultModel": "openai/gpt-5.5", "driftPaths": ["gateway.auth"], "message": "Live gateway runtime config differs from disk for model/provider/auth paths; restart is required or pending."}` -- no fingerprint fields.
- Text mode: `Runtime config: warning (live gateway differs from disk for gateway.auth; restart required or pending; live=openai/gpt-5.5 disk=openai/gpt-5.5)`.

Observed result after fix: the ok -> drift transition is visible on the normal read-scoped `openclaw health` path immediately after the disk change, with hot mode still warn-and-keep (live gateway kept accepting `sandbox-token-OLD`); the earlier caveat about the in-process snapshot-refresh handler masking external edits no longer reproduces on current main.

What was not tested: admin-scoped (`operator.admin`) live output with fingerprints (covered by unit tests `surfaces model/provider runtime config drift ... in sensitive snapshots` and `threads the admin scope into the cache-hit drift recompute`); live drift on the non-auth tracked paths such as `agents.defaults.model` or `auth.profiles` (covered by unit tests); the `{ cached: true }` respond flag is not printed by the CLI, so cache-hit routing of call 2 is established by the 60s window timing plus the deterministic handler tests.

target.title: fix(gateway): fail fast on missing local probe auth
target.body:
## Summary

Adds a fail-fast in `openclaw gateway status` for the local loopback case: when `gateway.auth.mode` requires credentials but neither the persisted token nor an interactive credential can be resolved, the status command synthesises a failed probe with a clear `failureReason` instead of attempting an anonymous WebSocket connection that surfaces as a misleading `Connect: failed`.

Explicit `--url`/`--rpc-url` targets are intentionally exempt: a user pointing at a remote, forwarded, or open gateway should not be blocked by missing local-config credentials.

## Details

- `resolveAuthForTarget` resolves through the probe-surface helper. When the result has neither token nor password AND the target is the known local loopback AND `gateway.auth.mode` requires credentials, it falls back to the interactive-surface helper and propagates the failure reason.
- The fail-fast is scoped to `surface === "local" && target.kind === "localLoopback"`. Targets with `kind === "explicit"` (i.e. `--url`/`--rpc-url`) skip the check.
- Tests cover both the local fail-fast path and the explicit-target carve-out, and isolate ambient `gateway.auth.token` env in the probe-auth test to avoid cross-test contamination.
- Review follow-ups (head `a4b92bef28`): when the missing-local-auth fail-fast synthesizes the daemon status rpc failure, the restart-health pass is skipped too, so `inspectGatewayRestart` no longer runs the unauthenticated loopback re-probe the fail-fast avoided. The unresolved-SecretRef warning is split so fail-fast results no longer claim "probing without configured auth credentials" when no probe ran.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: before this patch, `openclaw gateway status` against a local config with `gateway.auth.mode: "token"` but an unresolvable token (e.g. `secrets.token.env` points at a non-existent env var) would still try an anonymous WebSocket connection and surface `Connect: failed` to the operator. The operator-actionable diagnosis ("missing required local auth") was buried under a misleading network error. After this patch, the probe is short-circuited with a `failureReason` that names the auth shape.

- **Real environment tested**: two real runs. (1) Gateway status: `openclaw` runtime built from an earlier PR head on a local laptop checkout, run against an isolated test config at `/tmp/probe-test-68280/openclaw.json` so the live gateway and its real auth are not touched. (2) Daemon status: current PR head `a4b92bef28` (rebased onto current `upstream/main` `22376d80e1`) run from the source checkout via the repo CLI entry (`tsx src/entry.ts daemon status`) on macOS, with isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` pointing at a scratch state dir whose config sets `gateway.auth.mode: "token"` and `gateway.auth.token` as an env SecretRef (`MISSING_GATEWAY_TOKEN`, unset in the shell); no live gateway/service was touched.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  unset OPENCLAW_PROBE_NONEXISTENT_TEST_VAR
  OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/probe-test-68280/openclaw.json node dist/index.js gateway status --json | jq '.rpc | {ok, error, kind}'
  OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/probe-test-68280/openclaw.json node dist/index.js gateway status --url ws://127.0.0.1:18999 --json | jq '{rpc: .rpc | {ok, error, kind}, probeUrl: .gateway.probeUrl}'
  # daemon status path, at head a4b92bef28 (paths redacted to <scratch>):
  OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<scratch>/state OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=<scratch>/state/openclaw.json node_modules/.bin/tsx src/entry.ts daemon status
  OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<scratch>/state OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=<scratch>/state/openclaw.json node_modules/.bin/tsx src/entry.ts daemon status --json --timeout 3000
  ```

- **Evidence after fix**: Captured live from the patched runtime. The first scenario is the local-loopback fail-fast; the second is the explicit-`--url` carve-out.

  ```
  $ node dist/index.js gateway status --json | jq '.rpc | {ok, error, kind}'
  {
    "ok": false,
    "error": "Missing gateway auth token.",
    "kind": null
  }

  $ node dist/index.js gateway status --url ws://127.0.0.1:18999 --json | jq '{rpc: .rpc | {ok, error, kind}, probeUrl: .gateway.probeUrl}'
  {
    "rpc": {
      "ok": false,
      "error": "connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:18999",
      "kind": "connect"
    },
    "probeUrl": "ws://127.0.0.1:18999"
  }
  ```

  Daemon status path, captured at head `a4b92bef28` (redacted: scratch state paths shortened to `<scratch>`):

  ```
  $ openclaw daemon status
  Service: LaunchAgent (not loaded)
  Config (cli): <scratch>/state/openclaw.json
  Config (service): <scratch>/state/openclaw.json

  Gateway: bind=loopback (127.0.0.1), port=18789 (env/config)
  Probe target: ws://127.0.0.1:18789

  Runtime: unknown (Bad request.
  Could not find service "ai.openclaw.gateway" in domain for user gui: 501)
  Connectivity probe: failed
  Probe auth: gateway.auth.token SecretRef is unresolved in this command path.
  Probe target: ws://127.0.0.1:18789
    gateway.auth.token SecretRef is unresolved (env:default:MISSING_GATEWAY_TOKEN).

  Service unit not found.
  Service not installed. Run: openclaw gateway install

  $ openclaw daemon status --json  # rpc excerpt
  "rpc": {
    "ok": false,
    "error": "gateway.auth.token SecretRef is unresolved (env:default:MISSING_GATEWAY_TOKEN).",
    "url": "ws://127.0.0.1:18789",
    "authWarning": "gateway.auth.token SecretRef is unresolved in this command path."
  }
  ```

- **Observed result after fix**: in the local-loopback scenario, `rpc.kind` is `null` (no probe attempt was made) and `rpc.error` names the actionable auth diagnostic instead of a network error. In the explicit-URL scenario, `rpc.kind` is `"connect"` (the probe DID run) and the error is a real network-level `ECONNREFUSED` against the URL the operator supplied. In the daemon status scenario, `rpc.ok` is `false` with the synthesized SecretRef failure reason, `rpc.authWarning` no longer claims a probe ran ("SecretRef is unresolved in this command path" with no "probing without configured auth credentials" suffix), the gateway version stays `null` (no WebSocket probe was attempted), and no restart-health loopback re-probe runs after the synthetic failure (`status.health` is absent; covered by the `inspectGatewayRestart` not-called assertion in `status.gather.test.ts`).

- **What was not tested**: the explicit-URL daemon `--rpc-url` flag was exercised only via the unit test added in `a4b92bef28` (probe runs against the override despite unresolved local auth), not end-to-end against a live gateway. The restart-health pass against a live loaded service with a genuine (non-synthetic) probe failure was not exercised live; that path is unchanged and covered by existing unit tests. The compatibility question of shipping fail-closed behavior for configured-but-unresolved local credentials (ClawSweeper P1) is a gateway/auth owner decision and is intentionally not resolved by this contributor change.

target.title: fix(gateway): force exit on zombie shutdown + 503 healthz during shutdown
target.body:
## Summary

On rh-bot.lan at 2026-05-31 21:31 a gateway PID (71842) logged `[shutdown] completed cleanly in 5ms`, but the node process never exited. It held port 18789 for 2h13m. Every subsequent launchd-spawned gateway then took the lock-recovery path: probe `/healthz`, see 200 from the zombie, log `gateway already running under launchd; existing gateway is healthy, leaving it in control`, and exit 0. launchd's `KeepAlive.SuccessfulExit=false` kept new gateways down. The bot was offline for about 2h13m until manual `kill -9` plus `launchctl kickstart -k`.

The original SIGKILL of the parent process is the separate root cause documented in memory `project_rh_bot_isolated_session_sigkill.md` (`openclaw isolated-session` spawn pattern). This PR fixes the second-order defenses that should have prevented the zombie from blocking restart, not the SIGKILL itself.

## Layer 1: force exit after every clean shutdown

`src/gateway/server-close.ts:738` already logs `shutdown completed cleanly in Xms`, but a stray handle (HTTP keep-alive, telegram fetch, plugin native handle) can keep the event loop alive after every owned subsystem closed. `src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.ts:382` has an existing `armForceExitTimer(SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS)` safety net, but it only arms for `runAcceptedRequest` (signal-driven), not for the `closeOnStartupFailure` path in `src/gateway/server.impl.ts:1059`. That gap is exactly the rh-bot incident shape.

This PR adds `armGatewayPostShutdownExitWatchdog` in `server-close.ts`. After "completed cleanly" is logged, an unref'd `setTimeout` is armed (default 5_000ms, configurable via `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_POST_SHUTDOWN_EXIT_TIMEOUT_MS`). When it fires:
- emit a structured `shutdownLog.warn` with the active-handle constructor summary (via `process._getActiveHandles` or `getActiveResourcesInfo`)
- record the `gateway.shutdown.zombie_detected` restart trace event for OTel/Loki
- call `process.exit(0)`

Because the timer is unref'd, a healthy natural exit always wins. The watchdog only fires when something else holds the loop open. The injected callback shape (`armPostShutdownExitWatchdog` parameter on `createGatewayCloseHandler`) keeps vitest workers from killing themselves during the suite.

## Layer 2: 503 on /healthz during shutdown, plus tighter preflight

The deployed `handleGatewayProbeRequest` in `src/gateway/server-http.ts` returns 200 unconditionally for `/healthz`. A zombie still holding its HTTP listener therefore answers 200, and `probeGatewayHealthz` in `src/cli/gateway-cli/run.ts:369` accepts it as healthy (success criterion was `statusCode < 500`). The lock-recovery loop then logs `gateway already running under launchd; existing gateway is healthy, leaving it in control` and returns void to the supervisor, which respawns nothing.

This PR adds a module-level shutting-down flag in `server-close.ts`, flipped to `shutting_down` at the start of the close handler (before any await). `handleGatewayProbeRequest` consults that flag via injectable `getShuttingDown` accessor (defaults to `isGatewayShuttingDown`). When live probes (`/health`, `/healthz`) run while shutting down, they return 503 with body `{ "live": false, "phase": "shutting_down" }`. A `gateway.healthz.shutting_down_response` warn log fires once per shutdown sequence so the cascade is queryable in Loki without spamming.

`probeGatewayHealthz` is tightened to accept only `statusCode === 200`. The previous `< 500` admitted the new 503 (and any 4xx misconfig), defeating the layer 2 purpose. The lock-recovery loop now also emits `gateway.preflight.zombie_detected` (warn log plus restart trace event) when the lock is held but the probe is unhealthy, so subsequent supervisor cycles can be correlated.

The flag resets at the start of `startGatewayServer` so the in-process restart path returns to a `running` state before `/healthz` starts answering 200 again.

## OTel / Loki instrumentation

All four events emit via the existing `gatewayLog`/`shutdownLog`/`gatewayProbeLog` subsystems plus `recordGatewayRestartTrace`:

- `gateway.shutdown.zombie_detected` (Layer 1 trace) when the post-shutdown watchdog fires
- `gateway.healthz.shutting_down_response` (Layer 2 warn log) when /healthz returns 503 during shutdown
- `gateway.preflight.zombie_detected` (Layer 2 warn log + trace) when supervised lock recovery sees a held lock but an unhealthy probe
- the existing `restart.close.total` trace already covers clean-path shutdown completion

No new export plumbing is needed; the existing diagnostics-otel / Loki shipper consumes these events.

## Verification

Local Vitest with the patch applied:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server-close.test.ts src/gateway/server-http.probe.test.ts src/gateway/probe.close-drain.test.ts src/gateway/server.preauth-hardening.test.ts src/cli/gateway-cli/run.supervised-lock.test.ts

Behavior addressed: gateway zombie shutdown that left rh-bot offline 2h13m on 2026-05-31. With this PR the watchdog forces `process.exit(0)` so launchd reaps the PID, and `/healthz` returns 503 during shutdown so the next supervisor cycle does not defer to a draining instance.

The deployed bundle is the exact code that exhibited the bug; the proof script exercises both the deployed predicate and the patched predicate against real HTTP servers, plus the watchdog state machine.

[PASS] case4 watchdog warn log names the timeout in ms :: gateway shutdown completed but node process still alive after 50ms; forcing process.exit(0)

[PASS] case6b healthz returns 503 live:false phase:shutting_down when shutdown started :: {"statusCode":503,"body":{"live":false,"phase":"shutting_down"}}

Cases 4 and 5 confirm the watchdog forces exit on the deployed Node runtime and stops cleanly when cancelled. Cases 6a and 6b confirm the healthz state machine returns the canonical 200 ok body when running and the 503 `{ live: false, phase: "shutting_down" }` body the moment the shutdown flag is set.

target.title: fix(agents): bound GitHub release API response read in tools-manager
target.body:
Closes #103189

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the `getLatestVersion` function in the agent tools-manager calls `response.json()` with no size limit against the GitHub releases API. While GitHub release JSON responses are typically 36–60 KB, the call has no guard against an oversized or malicious response.

The initial 64 KiB cap was too tight: measured ripgrep payloads are ~50–60 KB (28 assets), leaving minimal headroom for routine GitHub release metadata growth.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replaced `await response.json()` with a content-length pre-check plus `readResponseWithLimit(response, 1 * 1024 * 1024)` and explicit `JSON.parse`. The 1 MiB cap provides substantial headroom over both measured payloads (ripgrep ~50 KB, fd ~37 KB) while still bounding the read. The content-length guard mirrors the bounded `downloadFile` pattern already present in the same file. The imported `readResponseWithLimit` is the same helper used across the codebase for capped HTTP response reads.

Risk: if GitHub's release JSON ever exceeds 1 MiB (extremely unlikely — current payloads are <6% of cap), `getLatestVersion` will throw and `ensureTool` will fall through to `undefined`, meaning the agent's fd/ripgrep helpers are unavailable until the cap is raised. This is a controlled failure mode that prevents an unbounded read.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. The GitHub release version check now has the same bounded-read defense that the download path already applies.

## Evidence

**Premise: unbounded read on current main**

```sh
git show upstream/main:src/agents/utils/tools-manager.ts | sed -n '156,163p'
#     const data = (await response.json()) as { tag_name: string };
#     return data.tag_name.replace(/^v/, "");
```

The `response.json()` call has no size limit. While GitHub release JSON is typically small, there's no guard.

**Live payload measurement (2026-07-10)**

```
=== Tools-manager release JSON cap proof ===
Cap: 1,048,576 bytes (1 MiB)

fd (sharkdp/fd):
  version:       v10.4.2
  actual body:   36,756 bytes
  assets:        21
  cap usage:     3.5%
  headroom:      96.5%
  within cap:    YES ✓

ripgrep (BurntSushi/ripgrep):
  version:       15.1.0
  actual body:   50,552 bytes
  assets:        28
  cap usage:     4.8%
  headroom:      95.2%
  within cap:    YES ✓
```

Both live payloads are well within the 1 MiB cap (>95% headroom). GitHub release endpoint: `https://api.github.com/repos/<repo>/releases/latest` (no auth required for public repos).

**After: bounded read with cap overflow guard**

- Content-length pre-check rejects declared sizes >1 MiB before reading the body
- `readResponseWithLimit` streams the body under the 1 MiB cap, cancelling the reader on overflow
- Same bounded-read pattern already used by `downloadFile` in the same file (line 186+)

**Focused tests**

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/utils/tools-manager.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  11 passed (11)
```

All 8 existing tests pass unchanged. Three new tests cover:
1. Declared content-length >1 MiB rejected before reading (body cancelled, guarded fetch released)
2. Oversized body stream without content-length cancelled by the stream reader on overflow
3. Normal realistic ~60 KB release JSON (matching ripgrep scale) parses through to download

**Module load verification**

```
node --import tsx -e "import { ensureTool } from './src/agents/utils/tools-manager.js'; console.log(typeof ensureTool)"
# function
```

Module loads with real `readResponseWithLimit` import from `../../infra/http-body.js`.

**What was not tested:** Live authenticated `ensureTool` end-to-end path that downloads and extracts fd/ripgrep binaries. Live GitHub API fetch shown above exercises the same `fetch()` path used by `getLatestVersion` for release metadata, but the full download+extract flow was not run in this checkout.

AI-assisted. Real behavior proof collected by human.

target.title: fix(android): show Canvas outside Settings
target.body:
Related: #101859

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Android users invoking `canvas.present`, `canvas.navigate`, or A2UI commands while outside the Settings Screen view would receive a successful command result without a usable visible Canvas surface.

This addresses the Canvas portion of #101859. It does not change camera or location command exposure, permissions, or gateway authorization policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Canvas presentation is now owned by the app shell through one retained WebView host with explicit unmounted, hidden, and visible states. Commands are serialized through that host, A2UI content requests presentation, Settings controls the same host instead of embedding a second one, and renderer recovery replaces a crashed WebView without replaying the crashing URL.

The shell also owns safe drawing bounds and Canvas background coverage, so content respects system insets without exposing the underlying app at the edges.

## User Impact

Android Canvas and A2UI content can now appear from Home and other app surfaces, hide cleanly through Back or close actions, survive rotation, and recover after renderer loss. Hidden Canvas state no longer blocks interaction with the underlying app.

Canvas commands complete when the host accepts the operation rather than waiting for remote page loading, while background presentation requests continue to fail explicitly instead of creating a deferred overlay.

## Evidence

- Live Android 15 E2E: reproduced the detached Canvas behavior on the prior path, then verified shell presentation from Home, Settings entry and exit, system Back, close and hide, A2UI JSON and JSONL push/reset, external HTTPS navigation, snapshot capture, slow-page command completion, failed-page recovery, repeated present/hide cycles, and portrait/landscape rotation.
- Live renderer-loss proof: forced a Chromium renderer crash, observed one crash callback, verified a replacement scaffold, and confirmed the prior crashing URL was not replayed.
- Live inset/input proof: verified Canvas content below the status bar with covered gutters, then hid Canvas and navigated Settings through the underlying shell.
- Live lifecycle proof: verified a foreground-to-background race returns `NODE_BACKGROUND_UNAVAILABLE` and does not present later.
- Android instrumentation: `CanvasHostLifecycleTest` passed all 4 lifecycle and renderer scenarios.
- Android build: `node scripts/run-android-gradle.mjs :app:clean :app:assemblePlayDebug :app:assemblePlayDebugAndroidTest`.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx50d3119m1acwsr391k7fj1`: `corepack pnpm android:test` and `corepack pnpm check:changed`.
- Fresh pre-commit autoreview completed with no accepted or actionable findings.

AI-assisted: yes.

target.title: refactor(qa): migrate Matrix scenarios into QA Lab
target.body:
Stack 2 of 4. Depends on #101253.

## What Problem This Solves

Matrix QA scenarios and profile selection still live in the legacy `qa-matrix`
runner, so QA Lab cannot own or validate the complete Matrix catalog through the
same declarative flow system used by other channel drivers.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the Matrix scenario implementations, Docker substrate, and 94-scenario
parity catalog into QA Lab, with deterministic profile selection and
module-backed YAML flows. Keep `qa-matrix` as a thin CLI/registration shim for
the remaining stacked callers; workflow migration and package removal stay in
successor PRs 3 and 4.

## User Impact

There is no production messaging behavior change. QA maintainers get one
canonical Matrix scenario catalog in QA Lab, while the existing
`openclaw qa matrix` command and generic live Matrix adapter remain compatible
during the stack.

## Evidence

- Parity tests cover all 94 legacy scenario ids: 81 module-backed Matrix flows
  plus 13 intentional mappings to portable QA Lab scenarios.
- Profile tests preserve the legacy counts and explicit-only exclusions.
- Blacksmith Testbox focused proof passed 24 files / 232 tests across QA Lab,
  the compatibility shim, and the plugin SDK runtime surface.
- The real release-profile command passed 2/2 Docker-backed scenarios on
  Blacksmith Testbox: `channel-chat-baseline` and
  `matrix-allowlist-hot-reload`.
- Exact-head changed-surface proof passed all static guards and the full `tsgo`
  project build. The two lint diagnostics were fixed and rechecked with focused
  tests plus zero-warning targeted lint.
- Fresh autoreview completed clean after the fixes, with no accepted or
  actionable findings.

target.title: test(plugins): cover filtered bundle MCP servers
target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

Evidence after fix: Terminal output from the temporary real OpenClaw setup:

```text
Proof root: /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins install --link /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp
Linked plugin path: /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp
Restart the gateway to load plugins.
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins inspect vision-mcp --json
{
  "diagnostics": [],
  "command": "npx",
  "args": [
    "-y",
    "@vision-mcp/cli@latest",
    "serve",
    "--apps-root",
    "/private/var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp/apps"
  ],
  "cwdEndsWith": true,
  "toolFilter": {
    "include": [
      "capsule.*",
      "vision_map.snapshot",
      "vision_map.list_apps",
      "vision_map.list_workflows",
      "vision_map.describe_workflow",
      "vision_map.describe",
      "vision_map.detect_state",
      "vision_map.list_actions",
      "vision_map.describe_action",
      "vision_map.perform_action",
      "vision_map.run_workflow",
      "vision_map.verify",
      "vision_map.repair_minimal",
      "vision_map.export_trace"
    ],
    "exclude": [
      "vision_map.click_at",
      "vision_map.type_text",
      "vision_map.press_key",
      "vision_map.scroll",
      "vision_map.init",
      "vision_map.apply_patch",
      "vision_map.add_control",
      "vision_map.commit_*",
      "vision_map.harvest_session"
    ]
  }
}
```

Observed result after fix: OpenClaw linked the temporary compatible bundle, detected its bundle MCP server, preserved both include and exclude filter arrays, set `cwd` to the bundle root, and resolved `./apps` to an absolute path inside the installed bundle.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:

```text
node scripts/test-projects.mjs -- src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts --reporter=verbose
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts
git diff --check
pnpm check:docs
codex review --base origin/main
```

Regression coverage added: `src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts` now covers a Codex-compatible bundle MCP config with a filtered server and a relative `./apps` data root.

Validation results:

```text
src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts: 1 file passed, 8 tests passed
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts: All matched files use the correct format
git diff --check: passed
pnpm check:docs: Docs formatting clean; markdownlint 0 errors; MDX check passed; i18n glossary passed; checked_internal_links=4554; broken_links=0
codex review --base origin/main: No actionable correctness issues were found
```

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime behavior change; docs now describe existing bundle MCP filter behavior.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime change. The docs encourage narrow bundle MCP defaults for high-risk tool surfaces.

What is the highest-risk area? The docs could overstate which configured MCP fields bundle MCP entries support.

How is that risk mitigated? Existing runtime code already reads `toolFilter` from bundle-provided server config, existing runtime tests cover filtering behavior, and this PR adds loader coverage proving the bundle file path preserves the filter before runtime discovery.

## Current review state

AI-assisted: yes.

Next action: maintainer review.

target.body:
## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Step 1 — drop a nested dated memory file under `memory/2026-05/` with a unique token:

```
cat > ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku/memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md <<'EOF'
Recursive memory search proof.
Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
EOF
```

Step 2 — reindex the live agent's memory store:

```
openclaw memory index
```

Step 3 — search for the unique token to prove the nested path was indexed and is retrievable:

```
openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
```

Step 4 — on the PR branch checkout (`30f15f4e22`), import the modified descriptor/help modules at runtime via `tsx` and print the after-patch strings to prove the new `memory/**/*.md` wording is observable from a real runtime call site (not just the diff):

```
node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs   # imports FIELD_HELP and buildPromptSection from this branch
```

**After-fix evidence**: Terminal output from the installed `openclaw 2026.5.20` runtime on the live workspace, plus runtime-imported after-patch strings from this branch (absolute paths redacted to `~`):

```
$ openclaw memory status
Memory Search (main)
Provider: local (requested: local)
Sources: memory
Extra paths: ~/.openclaw/shared-memory
Indexed: 105/105 files . 933 chunks
Workspace: ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku
By source:
  memory . 105/105 files . 933 chunks
```

```
$ openclaw memory index
[node-llama-cpp] ... falling back to using no GPU
Memory index updated (main).

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

## Summary

- Problem: new Control UI dashboard sessions without a label/displayName fall back to raw session keys, making multiple new chats hard to distinguish.
- Solution: add a Control UI fallback that renders unnamed dashboard sessions as their local creation time.
- What changed: gateway session rows now expose `sessionStartedAt`; Control UI uses it for dashboard-session display fallback, with `updatedAt` as a legacy fallback.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): no persisted labels are written, no rename UI was added, and explicit labels/display names still win.

## Motivation

## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Step 1 — drop a nested dated memory file under `memory/2026-05/` with a unique token:

```
cat > ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku/memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md <<'EOF'
Recursive memory search proof.
Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
EOF
```

Step 2 — reindex the live agent's memory store:

```
openclaw memory index
```

Step 3 — search for the unique token to prove the nested path was indexed and is retrievable:

```
openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
```

Step 4 — on the PR branch checkout (`30f15f4e22`), import the modified descriptor/help modules at runtime via `tsx` and print the after-patch strings to prove the new `memory/**/*.md` wording is observable from a real runtime call site (not just the diff):

```
node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs   # imports FIELD_HELP and buildPromptSection from this branch
```

**After-fix evidence**: Terminal output from the installed `openclaw 2026.5.20` runtime on the live workspace, plus runtime-imported after-patch strings from this branch (absolute paths redacted to `~`):
